A forecast format with confidence, missing-evidence warnings, and explicit alternatives such as accept, defer, or accept-and-drop
A pendant interaction for naming the proposed commitment and paging through the short spoken tradeoff

proposals.user_asks: “Translate this conversation for me, quietly.” The pendant should listen only while I hold the button, speak a concise translation through my earpiece, and show the original plus translation on my Mac when I want to review it.
proposals.why_useful: This gives the owner a discreet language bridge in travel, work, or appointments without handing a phone to another person. The pendant supplies the intimate, immediate interaction; the relay supplies low-latency speech translation; the Mac preserves a readable transcript; and the browser can look up unfamiliar names or terms without exposing the whole conversation to a public search.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime for turn-by-turn speech recognition/translation and short spoken output; a cheaper background text model for transcript cleanup, speaker-turn grouping, and terminology lookup. Never send raw audio to the background model unless the owner explicitly asks for a transcript.
proposals.latency_budget: The first translated phrase should begin within 1.5 seconds of a completed utterance; short phrases should stream incrementally. Mac review can lag by several seconds. If network quality drops, the pendant should say that translation is unavailable rather than inventing one.
proposals.cost_estimate: Realtime audio translation dominates, roughly $0.01–$0.08 per minute depending on provider and audio duration; background cleanup and occasional public lookups are cents or less per session. Storage cost is small if raw audio is discarded after translation.
proposals.security_concerns: Conversation audio and translations may contain health, financial, or identifying information. Require press-to-listen, a visible LED/haptic recording indicator, an explicit per-session retention choice, automatic deletion of raw audio, and local-only mode for a user-supplied phrasebook. Do not retain or search third-party speech by default. Browser lookups must use only public sources unless separately authorized. Translation is advisory: for medical, legal, or financial conversations, label uncertainty and offer the original transcript rather than silently substituting it.
missing: A translation session protocol with hold-to-talk boundaries, language selection, interruption handling, and an honest unavailable state
Streaming speech-to-speech translation in the relay with timestamps and confidence/uncertainty markers
Pendant firmware support for a press-to-talk translation mode and a distinct recording indicator
A Mac transcript viewer that can pair original and translated segments and delete the entire session
A privacy/retention gate that prevents raw third-party audio from entering routine memory
Optional terminology lookup that asks before sending a phrase or name to browser search

proposals.user_asks: “If I say I’ll do something, remember the promise, figure out the next concrete step, and bring it back to me at the right moment—without nagging me.”
proposals.why_useful: People routinely make commitments in passing and then lose them. This would turn a spoken promise into a small, reviewable loop: detect it on the pendant, preserve the exact words and uncertainty, use the Mac/calendar/browser to identify a realistic next step or deadline, and resurface it only when context makes sense. It is deliberately not an auto-task creator: ambiguous commitments become a one-tap/one-sentence confirmation request.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime model only for the short utterance classification and clarification; a cheaper background model compiles the commitment, searches permitted calendar/mail/browser context, and schedules follow-up. The final reminder is a concise cached audio item, not a fresh expensive turn.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge locally/server-side in under 500 ms (“I’ll hold onto that”) and ask clarification only when needed. Background enrichment may take 1–3 minutes. Resurfacing must be quiet-hours and attention-policy aware, with a snooze/stop response under 1 second.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.001–$0.01 per spoken commitment for classification plus background enrichment; most cost is avoided by storing a compact transcript span and only invoking the slower model when a deadline, person, or next step is missing.
proposals.security_concerns: Commitment audio/transcript is sensitive and should retain only a bounded transcript span plus structured fields, with expiry and deletion controls. Mail, calendar, and logged-in pages must be read-only unless separately approved. Never infer a promise from private audio without showing the quoted evidence; never contact another person or create an external submission automatically. Secret-like content must be excluded from reminders.
missing: A durable commitment record with quoted evidence, confidence, status (tentative/accepted/done/abandoned), and expiry
Cross-surface enrichment that can query calendar, mail, browser sessions, and local files while retaining provenance
A policy-aware resurfacing scheduler with quiet hours, deduplication, snooze, and a universal stop latch
A review UI/audio queue where the owner can accept, edit, defer, or dismiss one commitment
Owner-granted audio/event persistence and the already-requested intent-continuity and attention arbitration primitives

proposals.user_asks: “Show me what I knew, what I had promised, and what changed when I made that decision.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the owner can get current facts or an action receipt, but not reconstruct the state of their life at the moment a decision was made. A provenance-preserving time slice would let them revisit a missed commitment, disputed detail, or forgotten rationale without relying on memory: the pendant’s spoken context, relay events, Mac files/calendar, and authenticated browser evidence are aligned into a dated, uncertainty-labeled snapshot.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap background model to index and summarize already-captured records; use the realtime tier only when the owner asks a spoken follow-up. Retrieval should return citations and quoted evidence before any interpretation.
proposals.latency_budget: Return a first compact timeline in 2–5 seconds from indexed records, then progressively add Mac/browser evidence within 30 seconds. No live crawling is needed unless the owner explicitly asks for a current comparison.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low ongoing indexing cost and roughly $0.005–$0.03 per reconstruction depending on the number of records; storage/indexing and provenance joins dominate, not realtime inference.
proposals.security_concerns: This is unusually sensitive: snapshots may expose private audio, mail, calendar, browser pages, and secrets. Store structured facts and short evidence spans with strict TTLs, source sensitivity labels, per-surface inclusion controls, and deletion propagation. Never present inferred motives as facts; distinguish captured evidence, absent evidence, and model synthesis. Require confirmation before sharing or exporting a snapshot.
missing: An append-only, timestamped cross-surface evidence ledger that preserves event IDs, source, freshness, and deletion links
A queryable time-slice compiler that can answer “as of” questions without silently substituting current values
Retention and redaction controls spanning R2 audio, D1 jobs/memory, Mac workspace artifacts, and browser inspection records
A review view/audio format that speaks uncertainty and cites the original source without replaying sensitive audio by default

proposals.user_asks: “Before I act on an important detail, tell me if my sources disagree—and show me the smallest thing I can check to resolve it.”
proposals.why_useful: Current assistants summarize sources, but can quietly blend a stale calendar entry, an email, and a logged-in webpage into a confident false answer. The owner should receive a contradiction alert: exactly which claims conflict, which source is newer or more authoritative, what remains unknown, and one reversible verification step. This is especially valuable for appointments, travel, payments, deadlines, and addresses.
proposals.model_tier: Cheap background extraction normalizes claims and compares them; realtime is reserved for speaking the concise conflict and asking whether to verify. No model should resolve a conflict by plausibility alone.
proposals.latency_budget: For an explicit question, speak a provisional conflict notice within 2 seconds and complete read-only verification in under 30 seconds. Passive checks run asynchronously and notify only high-impact contradictions.
proposals.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.002–$0.02 per comparison; extraction and source reads dominate. Deduplicate unchanged claims and use hashes so routine checks are nearly free.
proposals.security_concerns: Claim records may contain sensitive account, travel, or health information. Keep source snippets bounded, label sensitivity, redact secrets, and avoid reading a private source unless the owner’s request authorizes it. Verification must be read-only by default; any correction or submission requires the existing confirmation policy.
missing: A typed claim/contradiction graph with source authority, timestamps, confidence, and materiality
A cross-surface read planner that can re-check only the conflicting fields in Mac, browser, and relay records
An impact policy that distinguishes harmless wording differences from conflicts capable of causing missed deadlines or financial harm
A concise pendant conflict-card/audio format with a one-step verification action and explicit uncertainty

proposals.user_asks: When a meeting starts, quietly get me ready, help me capture commitments during it, and leave me a reviewable follow-up packet afterward.
proposals.why_useful: Today preparation, live capture, and follow-up are disconnected. This would turn the pendant into a low-friction meeting companion: it uses the Mac's calendar and private browser context for preparation, the pendant for discreet capture while walking or away from the keyboard, and the relay to finish the packet after the meeting. It never sends anything without approval.
surfaces: mac-planner reads the next calendar event and gathers its agenda, attendees, related notes, and open browser tabs; browser-extension reads only already-open authenticated tabs relevant to that event and cites each fact; relay-realtime gives a brief spoken or LED-only pre-meeting cue and accepts short pendant utterances such as “commitment: send the estimate Friday” or “park that”; unified correlates utterances with the meeting's time window and participant context; mac-planner writes a dated meeting packet into ~/AI-Pendant-Workspace containing decisions, commitments, owners, due dates, unresolved questions, evidence links, and confidence; pendant plays a short post-meeting summary when the owner is available.
proposals.model_tier: Use the cheaper background model for pre-meeting retrieval, transcript cleanup, deduplication, and packet assembly; reserve realtime only for the brief cue and live utterance acknowledgement. Escalate to the expensive judgement tier only when owner, due date, or commitment attribution is ambiguous.
proposals.latency_budget: Pre-meeting packet ready 2 minutes before the event or on explicit request; pendant acknowledgement under 1 second; post-meeting packet within 2 minutes of the event ending. If calendar/browser access is unavailable, produce a clearly incomplete packet rather than inventing facts.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.05 per meeting for background extraction and summarization, depending on transcript length; realtime cost is limited to a few short turns. Mac and browser work dominate operational complexity, not tokens.
proposals.security_concerns: Meeting speech and private-tab data may leave the device to the relay/model, so default to local Mac notes and redact unrelated tab content. Do not infer or expose attendee-sensitive details beyond the meeting packet. Require explicit approval before sending follow-up email, creating external tickets, or changing calendar events; show source snippets and proposed recipients.
missing: A calendar-event identity and time-window correlation service shared by relay, Mac, and browser
A pendant capture mode that queues timestamped utterances offline and syncs them when the link returns
A meeting packet schema with provenance, confidence, owner/due-date fields, and a review UI
A reliable post-event trigger and availability check so the summary is not spoken during another conversation
built_from: GET /sessions and GET /sessions/:sessionId for authenticated browser context
POST /plan and POST /execute for planning and reversible Mac work
mac_run_actions (create_reminder, create_note, run_applescript) for packet creation
POST /pipeline/events and POST /pipeline/audio for event delivery and audio output
GET /jobs/:jobId and GET /jobs/:jobId/receipts for durable completion receipts

proposals.user_asks: Before I commit to a time, deadline, or promise anywhere, quietly tell me if it will make another commitment impossible and suggest the safest wording or alternative.
proposals.why_useful: People often make commitments in separate contexts—an email, a calendar invite, a private portal, or a conversation—and only discover the collision afterward. This would give the owner a last-second, evidence-backed judgment before a promise becomes real, while leaving the final decision with them.
surfaces: browser-extension detects a proposed date, deadline, recipient, or submission in the currently active authenticated page without submitting it; mac-planner checks Calendar, reminders, travel context, and existing reviewable commitments; relay holds a short-lived cross-surface conflict assessment and sends a discreet spoken or LED warning through the pendant when confidence is high; unified presents two or three feasible alternatives with the exact conflicting sources; browser or Mac fills only the chosen revised wording/time after explicit owner approval, then stores a receipt.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap background model to normalize dates and compare candidate times. Use the realtime tier only when the owner is actively composing or speaking and needs an immediate warning. Escalate ambiguous interpretation to judgement rather than silently blocking.
proposals.latency_budget: Warn within 1–2 seconds of a detected candidate commitment; if evidence is incomplete, say so and do not interrupt. A detailed alternative list may arrive asynchronously before submission.
proposals.cost_estimate: Under $0.01 for most checks with compact structured context; occasional long-page extraction may cost $0.03–$0.08. The dominant cost is private-context retrieval and browser/Mac orchestration, not generation.
proposals.security_concerns: Commitment data is highly personal. Keep raw drafts and unrelated page text local where possible, send only normalized candidate facts and minimally necessary sources, and never transmit or submit revised wording without confirmation. Do not infer obligations from sensitive messages unless the owner has enabled that source.
missing: A commitment candidate extractor that works on draft text and spoken utterances without taking control of submission
A temporal feasibility evaluator that distinguishes hard conflicts from movable commitments and exposes its evidence
A low-disruption pendant warning channel with suppression during conversations or quiet hours
A confirmation-linked mutation path that can revise the originating draft and record before/after provenance
built_from: POST /plan for candidate interpretation and alternatives
GET /browser/inspections and authenticated browser sessions for source evidence
mac_run_actions for Calendar/reminder inspection and reversible draft updates
POST /pipeline/events and POST /pipeline/audio for discreet warning delivery
GET /jobs/:jobId/receipts for the final provenance receipt

proposals.user_asks: “That’s not what I meant—fix the last thing you did.”
proposals.why_useful: Today an action receipt can tell the owner what happened, and some individual jobs can be undone, but a human correction often means “change the parameter” rather than simply reverse it. This gives the owner a spoken, cross-surface repair path: identify the referenced recent action, explain the proposed patch, and apply the smallest safe correction instead of forcing them to reconstruct the original workflow.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime for resolving the short spoken correction and selecting the recent receipt; a cheaper background model can compile and verify the patch. Execution remains deterministic on Mac/browser, with relay retaining the journal.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 1 second; show/speak the proposed repair within 5 seconds; execute reversible repairs within 15 seconds. Irreversible or ambiguous repairs stop for explicit confirmation.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.005–$0.03 per repair depending on whether semantic interpretation needs the realtime tier; most cost is receipt/context retrieval and any screenshot or page extraction, not deterministic execution.
proposals.security_concerns: Only recent owner-scoped receipts and the minimum related page/file context leave the device. Never infer authorization from the correction alone: sending, deleting, purchasing, or changing external records requires confirmation. Keep before/after values, tab URL, file path, and an undo token; redact secrets from the spoken response and dashboard.
missing: A durable cross-surface transaction journal that links Mac actions, browser mutations, and spoken intent under one repairable operation id
A semantic patch compiler that can turn “make it Tuesday instead” into a typed before/after change and reject unsupported repairs
A single confirmation/undo protocol shared by browser and Mac executors
Pendant delivery of a concise repair preview plus a local stop gesture

proposals.user_asks: “I lost my pendant. Lock it now, keep my information safe, and let me continue from my Mac without losing my place.”
proposals.why_useful: A wearable is uniquely exposed to loss, theft, or being left in a room. Today continuity and revocation are separate infrastructure concerns: the owner cannot quickly invalidate the missing device while preserving legitimate work context. This makes loss a recoverable interruption rather than a privacy emergency and prevents an attacker holding the pendant from replaying queued audio, invoking actions, or learning private context.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime only for the owner's short loss report and immediate acknowledgement; deterministic relay security code performs revocation. A cheaper background model can assemble a redacted continuity packet on the Mac after the lock is complete.
proposals.latency_budget: Remote lock acknowledgement under 2 seconds when the relay is reachable; queued local lock takes effect on the pendant's next wake or button event. Mac continuity packet available within 30 seconds.
proposals.cost_estimate: Under $0.01 per incident; dominated by one authenticated relay request and optional local context summarization. No recurring model cost.
proposals.security_concerns: Revocation must require a second factor or an already-authenticated Mac session, otherwise anyone who hears the wake phrase could cause denial of service. Immediately invalidate device tokens, cancel pending audio/action deliveries, erase volatile audio and sensitive cache, quarantine queued jobs, and rotate session keys. Do not copy secrets into the continuity packet; show exactly what was retained and for how long. Require explicit confirmation before re-pairing a replacement pendant.
missing: A device identity and key lifecycle service with remote revoke, rotation, replacement pairing, and replay protection
A pendant firmware panic/revocation state that survives reboot and refuses cached commands offline
A relay-wide kill switch for pending audio, browser, and Mac jobs scoped to one device identity
A redacted continuity export that transfers only active task state to the authenticated Mac, with audit receipts and expiry

proposals.user_asks: “Hold this for me until I have a quiet ten minutes.” The pendant should save what I said, have the relay and my Mac/browser gather only the relevant private context, and later give me a short cited audio packet with the decision or next step—without sending, submitting, or changing anything.
proposals.why_useful: This turns an interruption into progress instead of another forgotten note. The pendant is the only surface present at the interruption, the relay can keep the task alive, and the Mac/browser are the only places that can inspect private mail, calendar, files, and logged-in pages. It is deliberately preparation-only, so the owner gets value without an accidental commitment.
proposals.model_tier: Use gpt-realtime-2.1 only to capture/confirm the short handoff and play the final packet; use gpt-5.6-luna background jobs for evidence gathering and synthesis; use gpt-4.1-mini only for browser visual extraction if needed.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge the handoff on the pendant in under 2 seconds; background evidence collection may take 1–5 minutes. Deliver at the next owner-selected quiet window, or queue it durably if every surface is offline.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.02–$0.10 per handoff depending on browser pages and synthesis; realtime audio and repeated private-page extraction dominate.
proposals.security_concerns: Private mail/calendar/browser content stays on the authenticated Mac/browser path and only a minimized, cited evidence packet crosses to the relay. Never send mail, submit forms, delete, buy, or create external commitments without a separate owner approval. Expire raw audio and page captures quickly; show sources and an undo/clear control in the dashboard.
missing: A durable handoff record linking pendant capture, evidence jobs, and final audio packet
an owner-controlled quiet-attention window and delivery acknowledgement queue
a cross-surface preflight/recovery path when the browser is offline or evidence becomes stale
a compact provenance/citation format for spoken packets

proposals.user_asks: “Answer me privately; I’m in public.” The pendant should classify whether the reply contains sensitive information, keep private evidence on the Mac/browser, and deliver the answer through a private listening channel—or silently defer it—rather than speaking it aloud around other people.
proposals.why_useful: Today the owner must choose between getting useful assistance and exposing mail, calendar, health, finance, or work details to nearby people. This makes the pendant socially safe: it can still use the Mac and authenticated browser for rich answers, while the owner receives only an appropriately private rendering.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime model only for the live request and a short sensitivity decision; use the slower Mac planner for private-page retrieval and answer synthesis. A deterministic policy layer must override the model for secrets, authentication data, and owner-defined sensitive categories.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge mode selection in under 500 ms and deliver a short answer in under 5 seconds when context is already available. If evidence gathering takes longer, provide a neutral private “working” cue and queue the result without speaking content aloud.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.06 per request; private browser retrieval and synthesis dominate, not the sensitivity classifier.
proposals.security_concerns: Raw private page content must remain on the authenticated Mac/browser path; only the minimum answer crosses the relay. The device must never announce sensitive text while privacy mode is uncertain. Require a physical mode confirmation for ambiguous cases, provide a hard local mute/stop control, and log only policy decisions rather than spoken content.
missing: A product pendant with a genuinely private output path (bone-conduction, near-ear speaker, or encrypted paired earbud) and a local proximity/wear-state sensor
an authenticated sensitivity-policy evaluator with owner-editable categories and a fail-closed default
an end-to-end delivery acknowledgement that distinguishes privately heard, deferred, and accidentally audible
relay and Mac routing that keeps citations/evidence off the spoken/public channel while retaining them in the dashboard

proposals.user_asks: “Read me the brief. If I say ‘why?’, show me the source and let me open it on my Mac.”
proposals.why_useful: A spoken summary is otherwise a dead end: the owner can hear that something changed but cannot quickly judge whether it is real or act on it. Each audio item would carry a compact provenance token (source, capture time, freshness, confidence, and the exact supporting excerpt). Saying “why?” on the pendant retrieves the evidence, while “open it” uses the authenticated browser or Mac to reveal the original page without requiring the owner to remember which tab produced it. This is a genuinely joined behavior: the pendant supplies low-friction speech and playback, relay preserves the item identity, faculty-perception checks freshness, browser holds private sessions, and Mac presents the evidence.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime only for the short spoken answer and disambiguation; background extraction, excerpt hashing, freshness checks, and briefing assembly use a cheaper background model. No model call for a direct cached-source lookup.
proposals.latency_budget: Initial “why?” response under 2 seconds from cached provenance; source opening under 5 seconds when the browser bridge is online. If the bridge is offline, speak the citation and queue the open request rather than claiming it opened.
proposals.cost_estimate: Typically one small realtime turn for the spoken explanation; background extraction dominates but can use a cheap model. Direct provenance lookup is near-zero model cost. Browser/Mac execution cost is local/API latency, not inference.
proposals.security_concerns: Private URLs, excerpts, and account names must remain scoped to the authenticated owner and never enter generic logs or model context unless needed. Opening a source is reversible navigation, but any follow-up mutation remains gated by the existing confirmation policy. Never report a source as opened without a verified browser/Mac receipt; stale or conflicting evidence must be spoken as such.
missing: A stable briefing-item schema and provenance token that survives audio encoding, queueing, interruption, and reconnect
A read-only provenance lookup route returning source, excerpt hash, freshness, and confidence
A pendant utterance intent for why/source/open plus a resumable audio-item cursor
A browser/Mac verified-open operation with explicit offline/blocked outcome
A policy deciding which excerpt and URL fields may be spoken aloud

proposals.user_asks: “When your sources disagree, don’t guess. Tell me what conflicts, ask the one question that resolves it, and remember the answer for next time.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner currently gets plausible but unsafe answers when machine context, cached briefings, browser state, and remembered preferences disagree. This turns uncertainty into a tiny, actionable interaction: the pendant says the conflict in one sentence, asks only the minimum disambiguating question, and the relay records the owner’s answer with scope, source, and expiry. Future agents then stop re-opening the same ambiguity (for example, the authoritative timezone) and can explain which evidence they used.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime for stating the conflict and asking the one question; background model only for clustering repeated conflicts and suggesting a candidate resolution. Deterministic source comparison handles ordinary timestamps, reachability, and receipt states.
proposals.latency_budget: Conflict detection should add less than 300 ms to an answer when evidence is already present. The owner’s clarification is one short turn. Persist the resolution immediately; no Mac/browser round trip is required unless they are the conflicting source.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero for deterministic conflicts; one short realtime turn only when clarification is required. Background clustering is infrequent and cheap.
proposals.security_concerns: Never expose secret values while explaining a conflict; say “a saved private fact” rather than reading it. Store only the owner-approved resolution, its scope, provenance, and expiry. Do not silently overwrite a higher-authority fact; retain both claims and mark one superseded. Time-sensitive actions must remain blocked until resolution.
missing: A conflict object schema (claims, authorities, timestamps, scope, confidence, safe redaction)
A deterministic resolver that compares machine-context, browser, briefing, receipt, and memory evidence before model narration
A one-question clarification policy and owner answer route
Durable supersession/expiry semantics in the shared context projection
A pendant-visible acknowledgement that the resolution was saved

proposals.user_asks: “Why did we decide that? Reconstruct the short chain of evidence, assumptions, and approvals that led to it, and tell me what has changed since.”
proposals.why_useful: Today the system can perform pieces of research, planning, and execution, but the owner cannot later audit a consequential personal or work decision as a coherent story. This capability would let them recover the actual decision context: what the pendant heard, which private page or Mac document supplied evidence, what was uncertain, what the owner approved, and which later facts invalidate the conclusion. It is not an action-history list; it is a time-bounded, evidence-linked explanation of a decision and its present validity.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic event/provenance joins first; use the cheaper background model to summarize the chain. Reserve realtime for the owner’s spoken question and a concise answer, with drill-down only on request.
proposals.latency_budget: A cached decision packet should yield a spoken answer in under 3 seconds; reconstructing missing links may take up to 20 seconds and must be labeled incomplete rather than silently inferred.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low per query when event joins and hashes are available; occasional background summarization dominates. No need to resend full page contents or audio—store compact excerpts/hashes and retrieve originals only when authorized.
proposals.security_concerns: Decision chains may expose private mail, documents, or health/work context. Enforce per-source access at replay time, redact secrets and unrelated people, preserve immutable provenance, and distinguish owner approval from model suggestion. Never claim an approval that lacks a recorded owner event.
missing: A durable decision entity with links to claims, source snapshots, model suggestions, owner approvals, and resulting actions
Immutable, privacy-filtered event snapshots for browser pages, Mac files, pendant utterances, and action receipts
A change detector that compares the original evidence against current accessible sources and reports invalidation
A spoken drill-down protocol that keeps the owner on one decision while fetching a specific source or receipt
Retention and deletion controls that can erase a decision chain without leaving orphaned sensitive artifacts

proposals.user_asks: “Forget everything about that topic everywhere.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner should be able to revoke a sensitive conversation as a single intent, rather than hunting through pendant audio, relay jobs, browser extracts, Mac drafts, and derived memory. The system would first enumerate what it found, then delete or cryptographically tombstone the source recordings, derived summaries, queued jobs, browser snapshots, and local notes across reachable surfaces, reporting any unreachable residue and retrying later. This is a real cross-surface privacy power that does not exist today.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime only to identify the topic and confirm scope; deterministic entity matching and deletion orchestration should run in the background. Use a cheap model only to resolve ambiguous references, never to decide deletion scope silently.
proposals.latency_budget: Show a deletion plan within 3 seconds from indexed records; complete reachable deletion within 30 seconds, with durable retries for offline Mac/browser and a concise receipt when finished.
proposals.cost_estimate: Low model cost; storage/index scans and Mac/browser round trips dominate. Cost grows with the number of artifacts, not conversation length.
proposals.security_concerns: This is destructive and must require explicit confirmation unless the owner has separately enabled a narrow auto-delete rule. Never delete unrelated records from a fuzzy topic match. Keep a minimal non-content tombstone (identifier, scope, time, completion state) so the system can prove what was removed, while allowing the owner to erase even that audit marker under a stronger confirmation.
missing: A cross-surface artifact index linking raw audio, transcripts, summaries, context facts, browser snapshots, Mac files, and queued jobs
A deletion planner with exact-match/ambiguous-match classification and owner confirmation
Idempotent delete/tombstone APIs for relay storage, browser sessions, and Mac workspace artifacts
Offline retry leases and a verified deletion receipt that distinguishes deleted, unreachable, and not-found
A pendant intent and local pre-transmission cancellation path for newly captured audio

proposals.user_asks: “Tell me when my commitments conflict, and give me the least-painful way out.”
proposals.why_useful: Instead of separate reminders and briefs, the system would notice that a calendar promise, an email deadline, a travel reservation, or a logged-in task now makes another promise impossible. It would show the evidence and propose concrete options (move, delegate, decline, or ask for an extension), drafting messages but never sending them. The pendant can ask one short clarification at the moment a choice is needed; the Mac and browser do the evidence gathering that the pendant cannot.
proposals.model_tier: Background/slow model builds a normalized obligation and conflict graph from Calendar, Mail, local notes/files, and authenticated browser pages; realtime model is used only to explain one conflict and collect a choice through the pendant. Deterministic rules handle overlap, travel-time, due-date, and dependency checks before any model judgment.
proposals.latency_budget: Nightly and event-triggered scans may take 1–5 minutes. A newly detected high-confidence conflict should produce a queued capsule, not an interruption; once the owner asks, the first evidence-backed answer should be under 3 seconds. Draft generation may take up to 20 seconds.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.02–$0.15 per daily scan depending on how many private pages and messages are extracted; most cost is summarization and reconciliation, not rule checks. One realtime clarification is a normal short turn.
proposals.security_concerns: Private mail, calendar, files, and authenticated pages leave their surfaces only as bounded extracts with source, timestamp, and sensitivity labels. Never send, cancel, reschedule, purchase, or disclose without explicit confirmation. Conflicts involving secrets or health/financial data should be redacted in spoken output and linked to a Mac review workbench.
missing: A durable obligation schema with source citations, confidence, due/temporal constraints, and expiry
A conflict detector that distinguishes true impossibility from merely adjacent events and accounts for travel/buffer time
A ranked option generator with reversible draft artifacts and an explicit approval boundary
Event hooks from Calendar/Mail/browser watches into the detector, plus deduplication and quiet-hour delivery

proposals.user_asks: “Learn how I like things handled, but ask before you make a new rule.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner repeatedly says the same things—never send without approval, keep spoken replies short, defer low-urgency items, prefer reminders over email—but today those choices are scattered across pendant turns, Mac receipts, browser approvals, and dismissed briefings. The hive would infer a candidate personal operating rule from repeated behavior, show three concrete examples, and let the owner accept, edit, or reject it. Accepted rules would then make every surface less annoying without silently changing autonomy boundaries.
proposals.model_tier: A cheap background model clusters decisions and dismissals; deterministic counters and policy constraints prevent overgeneralization. Realtime is used only when presenting a candidate rule or answering 'why did you do that?'.
proposals.latency_budget: Learnings can be computed nightly or after 10 relevant events. Candidate presentation should be a 20–30 second spoken interaction, with a Mac review page for details. Applying an accepted rule is immediate and must be reflected in the next task.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually under $0.01 per nightly update; dominant cost is embedding/clustering a small decision history. No model call is needed for every action.
proposals.security_concerns: Behavioral history is highly personal. Store derived rules separately from raw transcripts, retain source references with short TTLs, and never infer sensitive traits or rules about health, relationships, or money. A candidate cannot widen permissions or authorize irreversible actions; owner confirmation is mandatory and revocation must be one utterance.
missing: A versioned preference/policy registry with scope (surface/task), confidence, examples, expiry, and revocation
A decision-outcome event stream covering pendant acknowledgments, Mac receipts, browser approvals, and briefing dismissals
A conservative rule learner that distinguishes stable preference from one-off context
A spoken-plus-Mac review and rollback UI with exact before/after behavior simulation

proposals.user_asks: “Help me negotiate this without committing me to anything.”
proposals.why_useful: For an incoming request, bill, offer, scheduling demand, or support dispute, the owner would get a private negotiation packet: what the other party is asking, what the owner has already promised, hard constraints from calendar and account data, plausible concessions, a recommended position, and a ready-to-edit reply. The pendant can ask one focused question about the owner's priority; the Mac and authenticated browser can gather the surrounding evidence. Nothing is sent or accepted until the owner approves the exact wording and commitment.
proposals.model_tier: A background model extracts the request and generates alternatives from cited evidence; deterministic checks identify existing commitments and monetary/date changes. Realtime is reserved for the short clarification and spoken summary, not packet construction.
proposals.latency_budget: A packet from already-open sources should be ready in 30–90 seconds; broader research may take several minutes. Spoken clarification should be under 2 seconds after the packet is available.
proposals.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.03–$0.25 per packet, dominated by reading private pages/threads and generating alternatives; deterministic constraint checks are negligible.
proposals.security_concerns: The packet may contain private correspondence, account details, and negotiation strategy. Keep raw source material on its owning surface where possible, transfer only bounded excerpts with provenance, redact secrets in voice, and require explicit confirmation for every outbound message, acceptance, payment, cancellation, or changed promise. Never infer a reservation price or disclose one without the owner's statement.
missing: A negotiation-specific packet schema for asks, constraints, concessions, authority, and commitments
Cross-surface extraction of the relevant thread/page plus the owner's existing commitments with stable citations
A consequence simulator that shows what each proposed reply would commit the owner to
A review UI and pendant interaction that supports edit, reject, or approve-exactly-this-text, with no implicit send

proposals.user_asks: “I’m in the middle of something—hold this thought, work out what’s needed, and bring me back to the exact next decision when I’m free.”
proposals.why_useful: Today an interruption destroys the thread: the pendant hears the intent, but the Mac/browser later lack the owner’s original reason, uncertainty, and stopping point. This would turn a spoken half-thought into a durable, cross-surface handoff. The pendant captures the intent and constraints locally; the relay preserves it while disconnected; the Mac and authenticated browser gather evidence or prepare reversible work; and the pendant later presents one short, sourced decision slate rather than replaying a long job result. It is specifically useful during commutes, meetings, and context switches, where no single surface can both hear the thought and finish the research.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only to capture/clarify the owner’s intent and to deliver the eventual one-sentence re-entry prompt. Use a cheaper background model for evidence gathering, summarization, and uncertainty labeling on the relay/Mac; use deterministic code for state transitions, expiry, and approval gates.
proposals.latency_budget: Capture and acknowledgement under 1 second when online, with an offline pendant marker immediately. Background handoff work may take minutes. On re-entry, deliver a 5–10 second spoken slate: what changed, what is blocked, and the single decision or next reversible action. If evidence is stale or identity/session changed, pause and say so rather than guessing.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.08 per handoff depending on browser/Mac research length; most cost is background model context and authenticated page extraction, not the short realtime utterances. Persist compact intent/evidence references rather than replaying full transcripts each turn.
proposals.security_concerns: Private browser content and local files leave their respective surfaces only as bounded excerpts and hashes; do not copy secrets into the pendant or relay. Require explicit confirmation for sending, deleting, purchasing, or other irreversible actions. Display source, timestamp, and what changed before approval; expire abandoned handoffs and provide delete-all. Treat a resumed voice phrase as intent clarification, never as approval by itself.
missing: A first-class cross-surface handoff object containing original utterance, intended outcome, constraints, uncertainty, stopping point, evidence references, owner-visible expiry, and current approval state.
A re-entry arbiter that chooses a quiet delivery window and suppresses duplicate prompts across pendant, Mac, and dashboard.
A typed decision-slate payload with cited evidence and a strict distinction between prepared/reversible and approved/irreversible actions.
An interruption-aware event path from the pendant that survives dropped links and reconnects to the same handoff ID.

proposals.user_asks: “Before you use my Mac or logged-in browser for this, tell me exactly what private information would leave my devices, remove anything unnecessary, and let me approve the smallest safe version.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner can currently approve an action, but not inspect or constrain the information flow that makes it possible. This gives them a practical privacy boundary across the hive: the pendant states the proposed data footprint in one short sentence, the Mac/browser perform local minimization, and the relay records only a redacted proof of what was shared. It is different from an action receipt or an irreversible-action confirmation: the decision is about disclosure before research or execution begins, including disclosures to the model itself.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic classifiers and field-level redaction for known secrets, contacts, tokens, and private-page regions. Use a cheaper background model to explain the remaining data footprint. Use realtime only for the short spoken disclosure summary and the owner’s approve/edit/deny response.
proposals.latency_budget: For ordinary requests, compute a disclosure preview in under 2 seconds and speak it in one sentence. If classification is incomplete, pause and label the unknown rather than silently transmitting. Redaction can add seconds to a browser or Mac job, but must happen before any model or remote service receives the content.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually under $0.01 per request for local deterministic scanning; $0.01–$0.05 when an explanation model is needed. The dominant cost is not the scan but any subsequent browser/Mac extraction, which should be reduced by sending minimized excerpts instead of full pages.
proposals.security_concerns: This is itself security-sensitive: the preview must be generated locally where possible and must not echo secrets into relay logs or pendant audio. Maintain an append-only disclosure manifest with hashes, categories, destination, and approval—not raw data. Require fresh approval if the destination, data category, target account, or action hash changes. Deny by default when a token, password, financial identifier, or unrelated person’s private content cannot be reliably removed.
missing: A preflight data-flow manifest spanning relay, model, Mac, and browser boundaries, with field-level redaction and destination labels.
Local secret/PII classification on the Mac and browser extension, plus a way to return redacted excerpts and proof hashes rather than raw captures.
A disclosure approval token separate from action approval, bound to the exact minimized payload and destination.
Dashboard and pendant rendering for a compact privacy preview, including an explicit unknown/blocked state.

proposals.user_asks: “Keep track of the things I promise people—including things I say casually—and, at the right time, remind me with the context I need; let me mark it done or prepare the follow-up without sending anything.”
proposals.why_useful: People lose commitments between a spoken aside, a calendar event, an email thread, and a private web task. The pendant can catch the promise at the moment it is made; the relay can preserve it when the Mac is asleep; the Mac and authenticated browser can later find supporting context and verify completion. This is a closed loop rather than another reminder: it distinguishes a promise from a thought, asks only when ambiguity matters, and gives a sourced next action without silently contacting anyone.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only to detect/clarify a commitment during conversation. Use a cheaper background model for nightly reconciliation, evidence extraction, deadline prediction, and drafting. Keep pendant-side capture deterministic and offline-capable.
proposals.latency_budget: Capture acknowledgement under 500 ms locally/relay-side; no blocking lookup during conversation. Reconciliation can run in 1–5 minutes after connectivity and a quiet-hours-aware check-in can arrive at the next useful moment.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.05 per commitment lifecycle, dominated by background synthesis and authenticated-page extraction; most spoken acknowledgements should avoid a model call. Storage is small text plus provenance; browser screenshots should be opt-in and short-lived.
proposals.security_concerns: Commitments may contain sensitive names, health, or work data. Store a redacted commitment and encrypted provenance, with per-source sensitivity and TTL. Reading logged-in mail/browser pages is allowed by the owner's policy, but sending mail, submitting forms, deleting data, or changing a calendar item requires explicit approval. Every reminder should show why it believes the commitment is open and which evidence it used.
missing: A durable commitment/obligation ledger with tentative versus confirmed state, owner-visible provenance, due-window and recurrence fields, deduplication, and completion/snooze semantics.
A cross-surface reconciliation worker that can join pendant utterances to Calendar/Mail/Notes/browser evidence without copying whole pages into prompts.
A local interruption gate and pendant delivery acknowledgement so a reminder is deferred safely when the owner is driving, speaking, or offline.
An approval-aware action compiler that turns a confirmed follow-up into a previewable draft and receipt.
built_from: POST /capture and GET /capture for immediate spoken commitment capture
POST /pipeline/events and POST /pipeline/audio for utterance and delivery event provenance
POST /briefing and GET /briefing/latest for a concise spoken queue
POST /routines and POST /routines/:routineId/run for reconciliation and quiet-hours scheduling
GET /browser/sessions, GET /browser/inspections, and browser command/result routes for authenticated evidence
POST /execute, GET /jobs/:jobId/receipts, POST /jobs/:jobId/undo, and POST /jobs/:jobId/cancel for previewable, reversible follow-up actions
GET /context-graph and /journal/:jobId for identity, thread, and action provenance

proposals.user_asks: “When I leave home, work, or another place I choose, quietly check where I’m going next and tell me what I need to bring, finish, or remember before I get there.”
proposals.why_useful: A calendar reminder says where an appointment is; it does not notice that the owner is actually leaving, reconcile the destination with open work and private web tasks, or catch the one item left behind. The pendant can provide the moment-of-departure signal, the relay can remain available when the Mac sleeps, and the Mac/browser can assemble a short, evidence-backed departure checklist from calendar, mail, notes, and logged-in reservation or work pages. This is proactive physical-world context, not another scheduled briefing.
proposals.model_tier: Use deterministic geofence and calendar matching first. Use a cheaper background model to compose and rank the checklist. Reserve realtime only for ambiguous spoken corrections such as “I’m not going to the office after all.”
proposals.latency_budget: A departure event should produce a useful checklist within 5–15 seconds, with a local fallback such as “You have an appointment nearby.” Background page reconciliation may take up to two minutes and must never delay leaving.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually below $0.01 per departure when calendar and cached context suffice; $0.02–$0.08 when authenticated browser extraction or synthesis is needed. GNSS checks and LTE-M bursts add battery cost, so use motion-triggered sampling and coarse geofences rather than continuous tracking.
proposals.security_concerns: Location history is highly sensitive. Keep exact coordinates on-device, send only a named place and coarse destination when possible, expire departure events quickly, and provide a hardware-button or voice disable mode. Browser/mail content must remain source-scoped and cited. Never send a message, alter a reservation, or buy anything from the checklist without explicit confirmation.
missing: Pendant-side GNSS/geofence and motion-trigger support, with coarse-place derivation that works during a dropped LTE link.
A privacy-preserving place profile store: named places, entry/exit rules, retention limits, and an owner-visible audit trail.
A destination resolver that joins place events to calendar and relevant open threads, then ranks only time-critical checklist items.
A local checklist cache and delivery acknowledgement so the pendant can speak a short fallback even when the Mac, browser bridge, or relay is unavailable.
built_from: POST /pipeline/events for departure and delivery provenance
POST /capture and GET /capture for owner corrections and one-off place notes
GET /machine-context and GET /context-graph for current destination and relevant entities
GET /briefing/latest and POST /briefing for the spoken checklist queue
POST /routines and POST /routines/:routineId/run for geofence-triggered reconciliation
GET /browser/sessions and the authenticated browser inspection/command-result routes for private reservation and work context
POST /execute and GET /jobs/:jobId/receipts for any explicitly approved follow-up action

proposals.user_asks: “Am I ready to leave?” Give me a 20-second departure check from my pendant: next calendar commitment and travel buffer, current weather, battery/connectivity, and any reservation or message that makes leaving urgent. If something is missing, say exactly what—not a generic failure—and never send or change anything.
proposals.why_useful: This is an on-demand life decision rather than another morning digest: the pendant is available at the door, the Mac can read private calendar/mail and device state, the browser can reach logged-in reservation pages, and the relay can fetch live weather and speak one concise answer. It turns scattered facts into a go/no-go check while preserving the owner's control.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime model for the short spoken synthesis only; use a cheaper background planner for parallel calendar/mail/browser extraction and cache stable facts, then hand the compact evidence packet to realtime.
proposals.latency_budget: Target 5 seconds from button/phrase to first spoken sentence; private-page extraction may take up to 15 seconds, with a partial answer immediately for battery/weather and a follow-up only if the pendant is connected.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.04 per invocation, dominated by realtime audio tokens; background extraction and cached weather/calendar normalization should be low-cost. Do not resend full page contents to realtime—send cited fields and freshness only.
proposals.security_concerns: Calendar, mail, and reservation data remain on the Mac/browser where possible; relay receives only normalized event time, travel window, urgency, and source timestamps. Never expose message bodies aloud by default. No external mutation. If a future version offers navigation, booking, or message actions, require an explicit confirmation phrase and show the exact change.
missing: A durable on-demand departure-check orchestrator that fans out to Mac state, AppleScript-readable Calendar/Mail, authenticated browser tabs, and public weather, then returns a typed evidence packet.
A reliable connected pendant trigger and delivery acknowledgement; the pendant is currently absent/offline.
Owner must reconnect the Browser Bridge for private reservation/account pages; current home-chrome is offline.
A location/travel-time source (Mac location permission or a configured home/destination and public routing provider) with a privacy-preserving coarse-location policy.

proposals.user_asks: “Let the pendant quietly tap me when something important is ready—such as a private browser result, a waiting approval, or a time-critical calendar change—and let me press once to hear the short explanation or twice to defer it. I should be able to use this in a meeting or on a noisy street without my phone speaking aloud.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner currently has no dependable private, glance-free attention channel: audio is inappropriate in many settings and the single LED is easy to miss. A tactile contract would make the whole hive useful in meetings, transit, and noisy environments while keeping the Mac/browser work invisible to bystanders. The same event can be acknowledged at the body, even when the phone or screen is out of reach.
proposals.model_tier: No realtime model for the haptic decision itself. A cheaper background classifier maps already-structured job/calendar/browser events to a small urgency taxonomy; realtime is used only if the owner presses to ask for the spoken explanation.
proposals.latency_budget: Tactile notification within 1 second of an event reaching the relay; one-press explanation begins within 2 seconds when the pendant link is healthy. Deferral must be local and immediate, even during a dropped link.
proposals.cost_estimate: Negligible model cost for event classification and compact push messages; occasional realtime audio cost only after an explicit press. Hardware prototype roughly $3–$8 in a production BOM for a coin/LRA haptic actuator and driver, plus modest battery impact (well under 1% per day for a few dozen taps).
proposals.security_concerns: Patterns must not encode sensitive content—only generic classes such as approval, urgent, or ready. Do not vibrate for message bodies or secrets. Acknowledgement and deferral events are private telemetry with short retention. Any approval that causes an external mutation still requires the existing explicit confirmation policy; a double tap means defer, not send.
missing: A pendant hardware revision with a haptic actuator, driver, and mechanical coupling that is perceptible on the wrist/clothing without being audible.
Firmware support for a tiny durable event ring buffer, pattern playback, local one-/two-press handling, and replay suppression across reconnects within the pendant's constrained RAM/flash budget.
A relay push protocol carrying event class, expiry, source, and opaque correlation ID, with idempotent acknowledgement/defer semantics.
A cross-surface event adapter so Mac jobs, browser results, and calendar watchers publish normalized attention events instead of each inventing notifications.
A small owner-facing pattern/quiet-hours setup and a safe default mapping, including a local universal-stop behavior for unwanted taps.

proposals.user_asks: Keep my pendant useful all day: when its battery or connection is getting weak, quietly move non-urgent work to my Mac or the relay, save anything needed for later, and only interrupt me if I must act before the device goes offline.
proposals.why_useful: The pendant is the one surface that follows the owner, but it cannot be the only place work lives. This would preserve briefings, queued requests, and follow-ups through battery drain, Wi‑Fi loss, or leaving the Mac behind—without making the owner micromanage which machine is awake.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap background model for forecasting battery/connection risk and classifying urgency; use realtime only for the spoken warning or owner conversation. The Mac/relay should execute deterministic migration and checkpoint logic without an LLM where possible.
proposals.latency_budget: Health scoring every 1–5 minutes; migration/checkpoint within 10 seconds of a threshold; spoken warning under 1 second once a genuinely time-sensitive item is identified. No warning for routine degradation.
proposals.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost for deterministic telemetry and queue migration; occasional small background-model calls for urgency classification (sub-cent scale). Main cost is durable queue/checkpoint storage and a few relay wakeups.
proposals.security_concerns: Battery, network, and queued-work metadata leave the pendant only to the authenticated relay/Mac; page contents and secrets must not be copied merely because a migration occurs. Require confirmation before migrating an irreversible action or sending anything; preserve owner-visible receipts and allow cancellation.
missing: Pendant battery/link telemetry exposed to the relay with hysteresis and last-known timestamp
A portable, resumable job checkpoint format with leases and deduplication across relay and Mac
Urgency/deadline metadata on queued work and a policy that distinguishes safe background migration from owner approval
A reconnect handoff protocol that lets the pendant retrieve a compact spoken summary and pending actions after an outage

proposals.user_asks: If I get interrupted halfway through something, save exactly where we were and let me safely resume it later from the pendant.
proposals.why_useful: Today a conversation, browser tabs, and a half-filled form can all be lost when attention shifts. This creates a durable, human-readable escrow: the original request, evidence gathered, reversible changes already made, exact next step, expiry/deadline, and what still needs approval. The owner can resume without repeating themselves or accidentally sending a stale action.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime model only for the brief spoken interruption/resume exchange and final approval question; a cheaper background model compiles evidence and a deterministic state machine validates and resumes the plan.
proposals.latency_budget: Capture interruption in under 1 second; resume card spoken in under 3 seconds. Background compilation may take minutes while the owner is away.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.05 per background packet, dominated by private-page extraction and audio generation; resume voice turn uses the normal realtime budget.
proposals.security_concerns: Private tab contents and draft data leave the browser only through the authenticated relay. Never persist secrets or raw screenshots by default. Sending, deleting, purchasing, or submitting remains a fresh confirmation. Expire stale packets and provide one-tap discard.
missing: A durable interruption-escrow state machine with explicit states (captured, awaiting-owner, stale, resumed, discarded)
Atomic checkpointing of Mac jobs and browser command queues so a checkpoint cannot claim an action that did not complete
A pendant-readable resume queue with offline acknowledgement and replay protection
Owner-visible packet diff showing what changed since capture

proposals.user_asks: When I leave something somewhere or put something on hold, let me ask later where it is and what I was supposed to do with it.
proposals.why_useful: People lose physical objects and the intention attached to them, not just the objects themselves. A quick pendant button press or spoken 'remember this' would create a private, time-and-place memory; later the pendant can answer 'where are my passport and the forms I still need to send?' instead of forcing the owner to reconstruct the moment.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime only for capture confirmation and the later short answer. A cheaper background model performs entity linking and summarizes the memory; vision runs only when the owner explicitly asks to inspect a photo or scene.
proposals.latency_budget: Capture acknowledgement under 500 ms locally, even without connectivity. Retrieval answer under 3 seconds when online; offline retrieval from the pendant's recent index under 1 second.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.005–$0.03 per memory after capture, dominated by optional transcription/vision embedding; negligible cost for offline text-only entries.
proposals.security_concerns: This can reveal home layout, possessions, travel documents, and locations. Store recent entries encrypted, default to coarse location and short retention, never upload a scene/photo without explicit consent, and require confirmation before sharing a location or acting on an attached intention.
missing: A pendant-local encrypted memory capsule with button-triggered audio/text capture and bounded retention
A cross-surface entity-and-intention linker that can join a spoken capture to Mac notes, calendar, email, browser pages, and optional photos
An owner-facing retrieval UI that shows provenance (capture time, place, transcript/photo) and lets the owner correct or delete it
Optional low-power BLE/UWB tags or phone-assisted location if the owner wants reliable object location rather than remembered placement

proposals.user_asks: “I’m leaving—pack up what I’m doing so I can continue from the pendant, and pick it back up when I return.”
proposals.why_useful: Today leaving the desk severs context: open Mac work, authenticated browser tabs, and half-finished plans are not converted into something usable while walking. This creates an intentional, privacy-bounded handoff: a short spoken queue for the commute, a resumable workspace on the Mac, and a clear return point rather than a vague promise that an agent kept working.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only to hear the short departure/return command and deliver the first acknowledgment. Use a cheaper background model to summarize the captured workspace and rank next steps; use the local Mac planner for app/browser state and no cloud model for raw private page contents unless the owner permits it.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 1 second. Capture Mac/browser state in 5–15 seconds, produce a 30–90 second audio queue in under 60 seconds, and make the return workspace available as soon as the Mac reconnects. Offline pendant playback must not wait for the Mac.
proposals.cost_estimate: One small background summarization per handoff (roughly a few cents or less depending on transcript/page volume); realtime cost is limited to two short utterances. Dominant costs are private-page extraction and audio generation, not orchestration.
proposals.security_concerns: Snapshot only the active window, selected browser tabs, task text, and provenance—not arbitrary screenshots or full page bodies. Redact secrets and mark authenticated excerpts as private. Never send mail, submit forms, or alter files as part of packing. Returning may reopen sensitive tabs, so require a local button press or spoken confirmation if the snapshot contains private browser sessions. Expire the handoff after 24 hours and provide one-tap deletion.
missing: A first-class handoff snapshot schema tying Mac window/app state, browser tab/session IDs, plan/job IDs, and pendant audio-item IDs together
A local pendant queue/marker that survives a dropped link and reports played/paused/expired state
A return-time revalidation step that checks tabs/files have not changed before reopening or continuing
Reliable browser bridge connectivity and explicit offline behavior (current home-chrome is offline with pending commands)
A compact audio renderer/acknowledgment path with the negotiated 24-kHz profile

proposals.user_asks: “Stay with me quietly in this conversation. When I ask you something, check my private notes and logged-in work pages, then whisper only a short, sourced answer through the pendant.”
proposals.why_useful: The owner can participate in a meeting or conversation without stopping to search their Mac. The pendant provides the ears and discreet audio; the Mac and authenticated browser provide reach into private material; the relay keeps the interaction low-latency. This is different from a meeting brief or a background digest: it answers a question arising now, with citations and a deliberate silence when evidence is insufficient.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime handles the short spoken request and final one-sentence response. A cheaper background/local model retrieves and ranks notes and authenticated pages; the Mac/browser agents perform only read-only searches. Escalate to the expensive model only when sources conflict or the owner asks for synthesis.
proposals.latency_budget: Acknowledge within 300 ms and return a sourced answer within 3 seconds for cached/local notes, or 8 seconds for authenticated browser retrieval. The pendant must say 'I don't have enough evidence' rather than fill silence with a guess.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually one short realtime turn plus a low-cost retrieval/reranking call, well under a few cents per question; browser extraction and repeated audio delivery dominate, not the model reasoning.
proposals.security_concerns: Requires an explicit session start and a visible/audio recording indicator; default to no raw meeting-audio retention. Only search allowlisted notes and currently selected browser sessions, never arbitrary mail or accounts. Cite source title and freshness without reading sensitive excerpts aloud unless requested. Pause on a button press or the phrase 'quiet now'; never send, edit, or submit anything.
missing: A consent-scoped live-session envelope carrying the selected source set, expiry, recording policy, and pause state across pendant, relay, Mac, and browser
Low-latency read-only fan-out from Mac notes and authenticated browser tabs with typed citations and freshness
A speech-turn arbiter that suppresses duplicate/low-confidence answers and guarantees a concise one-sentence output
A pendant-local privacy indicator and stop latch that works if the relay link drops
The end-to-end negotiated 24-kHz audio delivery path, with explicit fallback metadata

proposals.user_asks: “Can I take this on?” When I mention a new request or opportunity, compare it with my real commitments and deadlines, tell me the tradeoff in one short spoken answer, and—if it does not fit—draft a polite renegotiation or decline for my approval.
proposals.why_useful: People accept work conversationally before seeing the collision. This would turn the pendant into a timely decision aid: it checks calendar, existing promises, open tasks, and the relevant logged-in thread, then makes the cost visible without silently committing or sending anything.
proposals.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only to capture the request and ask one clarification; use a cheaper background model to reconcile commitments and draft alternatives. Mac/browser agents retrieve evidence; the relay persists a decision packet and schedules a follow-up if the owner says “later.”
proposals.latency_budget: A spoken feasibility answer within 5 seconds when local context is warm; up to 30 seconds for authenticated browser evidence. If evidence is slow, say what is known, continue in background, and return a cited packet rather than blocking the conversation.
proposals.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.05 per evaluation depending on browser pages and draft length; browser extraction and re-sent context dominate, not the brief spoken response.
proposals.security_concerns: Read-only access to calendar, mail, task systems, and logged-in pages is needed; private snippets should stay in the relay's short-lived encrypted packet and be minimized in audio. Never send, accept, decline, or create a commitment without explicit confirmation. Treat deadlines and availability as uncertain when stale, and show source/time for consequential claims.
missing: A first-class commitment/obligation index joining Calendar, Mail, Notes, reminders, and authenticated browser evidence
A decision packet with evidence, alternatives, expiry, and explicit approve/edit/reject state
A cross-surface impact scan that detects schedule/deadline collisions and distinguishes hard commitments from tentative ideas
Owner-configurable workload assumptions (working hours, buffers, protected time, and what counts as an automatic no)

proposals.user_asks: “Who was that person I just spoke with, and what should I remember for next time?” After I explicitly mark a conversation as worth remembering, identify the meeting or contact from my calendar/Mac, assemble a private relationship card from what was actually said plus clearly separated public context, and make it available from the pendant before my next interaction.
proposals.why_useful: People lose valuable social context because names, roles, promises, and personal details arrive while their hands are occupied. This gives the owner durable, privacy-respecting continuity without requiring note-taking during a conversation. It must distinguish observed facts from inference and let the owner correct or delete the card.
proposals.model_tier: Realtime handles only the explicit “remember this” marker and a short confirmation. A cheaper background model extracts facts, links the conversation to a calendar/contact candidate, and summarizes public context. The relay stores the result and serves a short pre-meeting audio reminder later.
proposals.latency_budget: A local acknowledgement under 1 second; a preliminary identity candidate within 10 seconds; enrichment and relationship-card construction can take minutes asynchronously. Before the next meeting, deliver a 15–30 second spoken card.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.02–$0.10 per saved conversation, dominated by transcription, entity resolution, and optional web enrichment. Most retrievals should be cached and text-only.
proposals.security_concerns: Conversation audio and relationship data are highly sensitive. Recording must require an explicit local gesture or spoken confirmation, with a visible/haptic recording indicator and an immediate cancel/delete control. Never record continuously by default, never infer sensitive traits, and never send a message or expose the card to another person without confirmation. Public enrichment must be source-labeled and limited to the identified person.
missing: An explicit, local conversation-bookmark event with start/stop boundaries and a deletion window
On-device or relay-side short audio capture/transcription that can retain only the bookmarked segment
Calendar/contact identity resolution with ranked candidates and an owner correction flow
A relationship-card data model separating direct observations, owner-entered facts, and public sources with independent retention controls
A pre-meeting trigger that can deliver a selected card to the pendant without replaying private conversation audio

proposals.user_asks: Before you brief me or act, tell me what is actually true across my pendant, Mac, browser, and relay—flag contradictions and stale status instead of confidently repeating them, and give me one safe next step to repair each problem.
proposals.why_useful: Today the system can simultaneously report a completed/healthy workflow, an offline browser with queued commands, a stale pipeline stuck in processing, and a briefing claiming Calendar/Mail grants are missing even though the live permission snapshot says automation is granted. The owner needs a trustworthy decision, not a fluent synthesis of conflicting records.
proposals.model_tier: Background/cheap model performs claim extraction, timestamp comparison, and contradiction clustering; realtime is used only to speak the short, owner-facing verdict when requested. Escalate to the expensive tier only when contradictions affect an irreversible action.
proposals.latency_budget: Under 2 seconds from cached snapshots; under 10 seconds when refreshing Mac/browser/relay evidence. Never block an urgent spoken reply on a nonessential source.
proposals.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.01 per reconciliation using a small model over compact typed claims; occasional realtime speech dominates interactive cost. Storage is a few KB per snapshot/claim, with short retention for sensitive browser facts.
proposals.security_concerns: Authenticated page contents, mail/calendar metadata, and device telemetry must stay in the existing private surfaces; send only hashes/typed claims to the reconciliation layer where possible. Never expose secrets or infer that a queued command ran. Require confirmation before repair actions, browser submissions, mail, deletion, or replaying pending commands.
missing: A durable, provenance-aware claim ledger with source timestamps, TTLs, and status values (current, stale, contradicted, unreachable).
A reconciliation pass that compares /ops/status permissions against generated briefings and compares pipeline state against relay/device acknowledgements.
A spoken-safe formatter that suppresses contradicted claims and emits evidence plus a reversible repair proposal.
A repair workflow that rechecks preconditions immediately before action and records the resulting receipt.

proposals.user_asks: When something I asked for goes wrong or arrives late, explain the incident in plain language—what I said, which surface received it, where it stalled, whether anything actually changed, and the safest retry—without repeating an action automatically.
proposals.why_useful: A failed spoken request currently leaves the owner guessing whether the pendant heard it, the relay accepted it, the Mac acted, or the browser was offline. A causal timeline turns opaque failures and late deliveries into a recoverable decision, especially when the owner is away from the Mac.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheap background model to correlate event IDs, timestamps, receipts, and acknowledgements; use realtime only to deliver a one-sentence incident summary and ask for confirmation when retry could duplicate an action.
proposals.latency_budget: Return an initial bounded status in 1 second from stored events; complete timeline correlation within 5 seconds. If a source is unreachable, explicitly say so rather than waiting indefinitely.
proposals.cost_estimate: <$0.01 per incident for compact event correlation; no model call for simple receipt lookup. Storage is small append-only event metadata, with payload redaction and retention limits.
proposals.security_concerns: Do not include private page text, mail bodies, or secret command arguments in shared incident reports. Redact sensitive fields, preserve source-local evidence, and require confirmation for retries that might send, purchase, delete, or replay a browser command.
missing: A stable correlation ID propagated from pendant utterance through relay job, Mac job, browser command, pipeline events, audio delivery, and receipt.
A causal-state vocabulary distinguishing accepted, queued, started, blocked, delivered, played, expired, cancelled, and unknown.
A duplicate-risk checker and owner-facing retry preview.

proposals.user_asks: Before I commit to something, let me rehearse the consequences: check my calendar, current commitments, private messages, travel or account details, and active browser work; show what this choice would collide with, what it would make harder, and a few safe alternatives—without changing anything.
proposals.why_useful: The owner can ask the system to execute isolated tasks, but cannot yet ask it to reason about a life decision across all of the places where consequences are distributed. A rehearsal would prevent accidental overbooking, missed obligations, contradictory replies, and commitments made without seeing the relevant private context. It is advice and simulation, not autonomous action.
proposals.model_tier: Use a cheaper background reasoning model to gather and normalize facts and generate multiple scenarios; use the realtime tier only for the short spoken result and follow-up questions. Escalate to the expensive tier only when evidence conflicts or the decision has high stakes.
proposals.latency_budget: A quick rehearsal in 5 seconds from cached context; a thorough one in 20 seconds with fresh private-page checks. The pendant should give an immediate acknowledgement while the deeper analysis runs.
proposals.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.05 per rehearsal, dominated by authenticated browser reads and synthesis rather than speech. Cache stable obligations and only refresh volatile sources.
proposals.security_concerns: Keep mail, calendar, account, and page contents on their owning surfaces; pass typed facts and redacted excerpts to the judge where possible. Clearly label inference versus evidence. No messages, bookings, edits, or submissions occur in rehearsal mode; any conversion to action requires a new confirmation and a fresh precondition check.
missing: A read-only scenario/rehearsal contract that takes a proposed commitment plus constraints and returns impacts, uncertainties, and alternatives.
A cross-surface obligation model that links calendar events, reminders, messages, browser transactions, travel details, and active work without copying sensitive payloads unnecessarily.
