args.user_asks: “Tell me when my commitments conflict, and give me the least-painful way out.”
args.why_useful: Instead of separate reminders and briefs, the system would notice that a calendar promise, an email deadline, a travel reservation, or a logged-in task now makes another promise impossible. It would show the evidence and propose concrete options (move, delegate, decline, or ask for an extension), drafting messages but never sending them. The pendant can ask one short clarification at the moment a choice is needed; the Mac and browser do the evidence gathering that the pendant cannot.
args.model_tier: Background/slow model builds a normalized obligation and conflict graph from Calendar, Mail, local notes/files, and authenticated browser pages; realtime model is used only to explain one conflict and collect a choice through the pendant. Deterministic rules handle overlap, travel-time, due-date, and dependency checks before any model judgment.
args.latency_budget: Nightly and event-triggered scans may take 1–5 minutes. A newly detected high-confidence conflict should produce a queued capsule, not an interruption; once the owner asks, the first evidence-backed answer should be under 3 seconds. Draft generation may take up to 20 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.02–$0.15 per daily scan depending on how many private pages and messages are extracted; most cost is summarization and reconciliation, not rule checks. One realtime clarification is a normal short turn.
args.security_concerns: Private mail, calendar, files, and authenticated pages leave their surfaces only as bounded extracts with source, timestamp, and sensitivity labels. Never send, cancel, reschedule, purchase, or disclose without explicit confirmation. Conflicts involving secrets or health/financial data should be redacted in spoken output and linked to a Mac review workbench.
missing: A durable obligation schema with source citations, confidence, due/temporal constraints, and expiry
A conflict detector that distinguishes true impossibility from merely adjacent events and accounts for travel/buffer time
A ranked option generator with reversible draft artifacts and an explicit approval boundary
Event hooks from Calendar/Mail/browser watches into the detector, plus deduplication and quiet-hour delivery

args.change: Create a durable obligation-and-conflict event layer between existing context graph/research/briefing routes: normalize commitments from Calendar, Mail, local notes, and authenticated browser extracts into typed obligations; emit idempotent conflict events with source citations, temporal/travel constraints, confidence, expiry, and a ranked set of reversible options. Persist a draft-only resolution packet that the Mac workbench and pendant queue can consume, with explicit owner approval required for any external mutation.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets an early, explainable warning that two promises cannot both be kept, plus a ready way out, rather than discovering the collision during a meeting or after a deadline. It turns existing disconnected reads and briefs into dependable life coordination.
args.effort: Medium-high: schema and D1/R2 persistence, Calendar/Mail/notes/browser adapters, deterministic temporal rules, conflict deduplication, and a review/approval packet rendered by Mac and pendant. Start with calendar + browser deadlines, then add mail and local files.
args.risk: False conflicts could create alert fatigue; mitigate with confidence thresholds, quiet-hour queueing, evidence links, and a dismiss/merge feedback loop. Never execute a cancellation, send, or reschedule from the detector. If a source is unavailable, mark the conflict incomplete rather than infer absence.
args.cost_impact: Low recurring storage and rule-evaluation cost; background model extraction is the dominant API cost, approximately cents per scan. No new hardware required.
args.latency_impact: Event ingestion is near-real-time where hooks exist; reconciliation is seconds to minutes. Spoken delivery waits for a stable packet and should remain under 3 seconds after it is queued.
args.security_impact: Sensitive source text stays bounded and provenance-tagged; spoken output uses redacted summaries. Approval packets must preserve the exact before/after effect and source evidence, and expired source extracts must be deleted on the retention policy.
depends_on: Durable typed context projection rather than hand-written fleetContext
Authenticated browser command/session reliability and truthful offline status
A durable review queue with acknowledgment, expiry, and approval gates
Calendar/Mail event or polling adapters on the Mac agent

args.user_asks: “Learn how I like things handled, but ask before you make a new rule.”
args.why_useful: The owner repeatedly says the same things—never send without approval, keep spoken replies short, defer low-urgency items, prefer reminders over email—but today those choices are scattered across pendant turns, Mac receipts, browser approvals, and dismissed briefings. The hive would infer a candidate personal operating rule from repeated behavior, show three concrete examples, and let the owner accept, edit, or reject it. Accepted rules would then make every surface less annoying without silently changing autonomy boundaries.
args.model_tier: A cheap background model clusters decisions and dismissals; deterministic counters and policy constraints prevent overgeneralization. Realtime is used only when presenting a candidate rule or answering 'why did you do that?'.
args.latency_budget: Learnings can be computed nightly or after 10 relevant events. Candidate presentation should be a 20–30 second spoken interaction, with a Mac review page for details. Applying an accepted rule is immediate and must be reflected in the next task.
args.cost_estimate: Usually under $0.01 per nightly update; dominant cost is embedding/clustering a small decision history. No model call is needed for every action.
args.security_concerns: Behavioral history is highly personal. Store derived rules separately from raw transcripts, retain source references with short TTLs, and never infer sensitive traits or rules about health, relationships, or money. A candidate cannot widen permissions or authorize irreversible actions; owner confirmation is mandatory and revocation must be one utterance.
missing: A versioned preference/policy registry with scope (surface/task), confidence, examples, expiry, and revocation
A decision-outcome event stream covering pendant acknowledgments, Mac receipts, browser approvals, and briefing dismissals
A conservative rule learner that distinguishes stable preference from one-off context
A spoken-plus-Mac review and rollback UI with exact before/after behavior simulation

args.user_asks: “Help me negotiate this without committing me to anything.”
args.why_useful: For an incoming request, bill, offer, scheduling demand, or support dispute, the owner would get a private negotiation packet: what the other party is asking, what the owner has already promised, hard constraints from calendar and account data, plausible concessions, a recommended position, and a ready-to-edit reply. The pendant can ask one focused question about the owner's priority; the Mac and authenticated browser can gather the surrounding evidence. Nothing is sent or accepted until the owner approves the exact wording and commitment.
args.model_tier: A background model extracts the request and generates alternatives from cited evidence; deterministic checks identify existing commitments and monetary/date changes. Realtime is reserved for the short clarification and spoken summary, not packet construction.
args.latency_budget: A packet from already-open sources should be ready in 30–90 seconds; broader research may take several minutes. Spoken clarification should be under 2 seconds after the packet is available.
args.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.03–$0.25 per packet, dominated by reading private pages/threads and generating alternatives; deterministic constraint checks are negligible.
args.security_concerns: The packet may contain private correspondence, account details, and negotiation strategy. Keep raw source material on its owning surface where possible, transfer only bounded excerpts with provenance, redact secrets in voice, and require explicit confirmation for every outbound message, acceptance, payment, cancellation, or changed promise. Never infer a reservation price or disclose one without the owner's statement.
missing: A negotiation-specific packet schema for asks, constraints, concessions, authority, and commitments
Cross-surface extraction of the relevant thread/page plus the owner's existing commitments with stable citations
A consequence simulator that shows what each proposed reply would commit the owner to

args.change: Add a negotiation-packet compiler and consequence simulator that accepts a cited incoming request from Mail/browser, resolves only the owner's relevant calendar/account commitments, and produces three explicitly labeled reply variants (accept, counter, decline). args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can respond confidently to difficult requests without manually reconstructing context or accidentally agreeing to something hidden in a polished draft. They see the consequences before committing and can approve only the exact reply they intend.
args.effort: Medium: packet schema, evidence joiner, deterministic consequence rules, text/version hashing, and adapters for Mac Mail and authenticated browser forms; a Mac review surface and pendant summary are needed.
args.risk: The model may miss an obligation or misread leverage; expose uncertainty and source excerpts, offer no-answer/ask-for-time variants, and fail closed when evidence is incomplete. Version hashes prevent a later edit from being sent under an earlier approval.
args.cost_impact: Small persistent storage and hashing cost; roughly cents per packet for extraction and alternatives, with no recurring cost after approval.
args.latency_impact: Compilation takes tens of seconds for local sources and minutes for multiple private tabs; exact-text approval and send can be immediate once the packet is ready.
args.security_impact: Sensitive negotiations stay scoped to the selected thread and sources, with redacted voice summaries and short-lived packet retention. Approval tokens are single-use, audience-bound, and cannot authorize unrelated actions.

args.user_asks: “I’m in the middle of something—hold this thought, work out what’s needed, and bring me back to the exact next decision when I’m free.”
args.why_useful: Today an interruption destroys the thread: the pendant hears the intent, but the Mac/browser later lack the owner’s original reason, uncertainty, and stopping point. This would turn a spoken half-thought into a durable, cross-surface handoff. The pendant captures the intent and constraints locally; the relay preserves it while disconnected; the Mac and authenticated browser gather evidence or prepare reversible work; and the pendant later presents one short, sourced decision slate rather than replaying a long job result. It is specifically useful during commutes, meetings, and context switches, where no single surface can both hear the thought and finish the research.
args.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only to capture/clarify the owner’s intent and to deliver the eventual one-sentence re-entry prompt. Use a cheaper background model for evidence gathering, summarization, and uncertainty labeling on the relay/Mac; use deterministic code for state transitions, expiry, and approval gates.
args.latency_budget: Capture and acknowledgement under 1 second when online, with an offline pendant marker immediately. Background handoff work may take minutes. On re-entry, deliver a 5–10 second spoken slate: what changed, what is blocked, and the single decision or next reversible action. If evidence is stale or identity/session changed, pause and say so rather than guessing.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.08 per handoff depending on browser/Mac research length; most cost is background model context and authenticated page extraction, not the short realtime utterances. Persist compact intent/evidence references rather than replaying full transcripts each turn.
args.security_concerns: Private browser content and local files leave their respective surfaces only as bounded excerpts and hashes; do not copy secrets into the pendant or relay. Require explicit confirmation for sending, deleting, purchasing, or other irreversible actions. Display source, timestamp, and what changed before approval; expire abandoned handoffs and provide delete-all. Treat a resumed voice phrase as intent clarification, never as approval by itself.
missing: A first-class cross-surface handoff object containing original utterance, intended outcome, constraints, uncertainty, stopping point, evidence references, owner-visible expiry, and current approval state.
A re-entry arbiter that chooses a quiet delivery window and suppresses duplicate prompts across pendant, Mac, and dashboard.
A typed decision-slate payload with cited evidence and a strict distinction between prepared/reversible and approved/irreversible actions.
An interruption-aware event path from the pendant that survives dropped links and reconnects to the same handoff ID.

args.change: Add a durable Handoff Envelope and Re-entry Arbiter between the existing event/capture, job, browser, and execution paths. On a pendant interruption, create one handoffId with the raw intent reference, normalized goal, constraints, uncertainty, stopping point, owner timezone/quiet hours, and expiry. Every downstream job, browser extraction, and prepared action must attach that handoffId and append typed evidence (source, timestamp, freshness, confidence) rather than returning an unlinked result. On reconnect or a chosen quiet window, the arbiter compiles a 3-field decision slate—what changed, what is blocked, next reversible step—and routes exactly one delivery to the pendant or Mac. Approval is a separate state transition; execution receipts and undo references close the same handoff. Expire or cancel must fan out idempotently to jobs and queued audio.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can say “hold this thought” once and later resume at the exact decision, even if they leave the Mac, lose the browser bridge, or cross an offline interval. They stop getting orphaned job completions and repeated reminders, and never mistake prepared work for approved action.
args.effort: Medium-high: schema and event migration, idempotent fan-out/cancellation, one arbiter worker, and pendant reconnect handling; can ship read-only decision slates before enabling action execution.
args.risk: A stale or wrongly merged handoff could prompt the owner about the wrong task. Mitigate with explicit handoff IDs, source/timestamp display, confidence thresholds, owner confirmation on ambiguous re-entry, expiry, and a global cancel. If a downstream surface disappears, preserve the handoff as blocked rather than silently completing it.
args.cost_impact: Small durable storage and queue overhead; approximately one compact background-model call per handoff plus existing browser/Mac costs. No need to resend full transcripts.
args.latency_impact: Sub-second acknowledgement; background processing is asynchronous. Re-entry compilation should be under 2 seconds from fresh evidence, with stale evidence clearly marked.
args.security_impact: Keep raw private page text on the owning surface where possible; relay stores references, hashes, and minimal excerpts. Never place secrets in pendant audio. Approval tokens are single-use, scoped to handoffId and action hash.
depends_on: A typed cross-surface event schema with correlation IDs
A durable job cancellation/expiry primitive
A decision-slate and approval-state representation
A pendant reconnect/offline marker path

args.user_asks: “Before you use my Mac or logged-in browser for this, tell me exactly what private information would leave my devices, remove anything unnecessary, and let me approve the smallest safe version.”
args.why_useful: The owner can currently approve an action, but not inspect or constrain the information flow that makes it possible. This gives them a practical privacy boundary across the hive: the pendant states the proposed data footprint in one short sentence, the Mac/browser perform local minimization, and the relay records only a redacted proof of what was shared. It is different from an action receipt or an irreversible-action confirmation: the decision is about disclosure before research or execution begins, including disclosures to the model itself.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic classifiers and field-level redaction for known secrets, contacts, tokens, and private-page regions. Use a cheaper background model to explain the remaining data footprint. Use realtime only for the short spoken disclosure summary and the owner’s approve/edit/deny response.
args.latency_budget: For ordinary requests, compute a disclosure preview in under 2 seconds and speak it in one sentence. If classification is incomplete, pause and label the unknown rather than silently transmitting. Redaction can add seconds to a browser or Mac job, but must happen before any model or remote service receives the content.
args.cost_estimate: Usually under $0.01 per request for local deterministic scanning; $0.01–$0.05 when an explanation model is needed. The dominant cost is not the scan but any subsequent browser/Mac extraction, which should be reduced by sending minimized excerpts instead of full pages.
args.security_concerns: This is itself security-sensitive: the preview must be generated locally where possible and must not echo secrets into relay logs or pendant audio. Maintain an append-only disclosure manifest with hashes, categories, destination, and approval—not raw data. Require fresh approval if the destination, data category, target account, or action hash changes. Deny by default when a token, password, financial identifier, or unrelated person’s private content cannot be reliably removed.
missing: A preflight data-flow manifest spanning relay, model, Mac, and browser boundaries, with field-level redaction and destination labels.
Local secret/PII classification on the Mac and browser extension, plus a way to return redacted excerpts and proof hashes rather than raw captures.
A disclosure approval token separate from action approval, bound to the exact minimized payload and destination.
Dashboard and pendant rendering for a compact privacy preview, including an explicit unknown/blocked state.

args.change: Insert a Disclosure Preflight stage before /plan, browser extraction, model invocation, or /execute. It should build a typed manifest of every proposed input and destination (pendant, relay, model tier, Mac app, browser origin, external recipient), run local redaction on the Mac/extension, replace raw values with minimized excerpts or salted proof hashes, and issue a single-use disclosure token bound to the exact payload hash, destination set, and expiry. Downstream routes must reject requests without a matching token; any changed tab, target, field, or model destination invalidates it. Store only the manifest and approval decision in receipts, never the unredacted payload.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets a real, enforceable boundary instead of a reassuring prompt: private account pages, unrelated messages, credentials, and personal files cannot silently become model context just because a task crossed surfaces. They can approve a useful minimized request without choosing between total automation and total refusal.
args.effort: High: define the manifest schema, implement local scanners/redactors in the Mac and browser bridge, enforce token checks in relay routes, add safe failure behavior, and add compact pendant/dashboard rendering. Start with known credential/PII classes and expand classifiers after telemetry proves low false-negative rates.
args.risk: Over-redaction can make tasks fail or produce misleading results; under-redaction is a privacy breach. Fail closed for secrets and unknown destinations, show what was omitted, and allow the owner to explicitly widen scope by category—not by blindly forwarding the original page. Recovery is to re-run preflight after edits; never fall back to raw capture.
args.cost_impact: Low per-request compute for local scanning; modest storage for manifests and hashes. It may reduce model token cost by shrinking context, while adding engineering and maintenance cost for classifiers.
args.latency_impact: Adds roughly 0.5–2 seconds for local preflight; remote/model work starts only after approval. Cached classification for unchanged pages can make repeat requests near-instant.
args.security_impact: Strongly improves least-privilege and auditability, but the classifier and token verifier become security-critical. Keep manifests redacted, isolate keys, rotate token signing keys, and ensure logs cannot reconstruct sensitive values.
depends_on: A shared typed cross-surface payload manifest and destination taxonomy
Mac/browser local redaction and proof-hash services
Relay enforcement of scoped disclosure tokens
Owner-visible privacy preview and approval UI/audio

args.security_concerns: Commitments may contain sensitive names, health, or work data. Store a redacted commitment and encrypted provenance, with per-source sensitivity and TTL. Reading logged-in mail/browser pages is allowed by the owner's policy, but sending mail, submitting forms, deleting data, or changing a calendar item requires explicit approval. Every reminder should show why it believes the commitment is open and which evidence it used.
missing: A durable commitment/obligation ledger with tentative versus confirmed state, owner-visible provenance, due-window and recurrence fields, deduplication, and completion/snooze semantics.
A cross-surface reconciliation worker that can join pendant utterances to Calendar/Mail/Notes/browser evidence without copying whole pages into prompts.

args.change: Replace the prototype’s 15,625 Hz I2S microphone/clock path with a production audio front end that captures 24 kHz (preferably a 48 kHz digital MEMS mic plus deterministic decimation, or a native 24 kHz I2S clock), and carry an explicit audio-format contract through firmware, relay transcoding, and Mac playback. args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets genuinely clearer speech and more reliable recognition of names and consonants in noisy everyday use, rather than a 24 kHz label applied to narrowband input. Roll out behind a negotiated format bit and retain the current 16 kHz uplink fallback. If LTE-M power or CPU is unacceptable, capture at 48 kHz locally but downsample to a verified 24 kHz frame before encoding.

args.latency_impact: Potentially +5–15 ms for resampling and larger buffers; preserve 60 ms Opus framing and negotiate down to 16 kHz on weak links.
args.security_impact: No new data class, but higher-fidelity audio can reveal more ambient detail. Keep existing transport encryption, avoid retaining raw PCM, and make format negotiation and recording retention observable in receipts.

transcript.text:
This round produced two proposals:

1. **Commitment loop:** The pendant captures casual promises, the relay preserves them across disconnections, and the Mac/browser later reconcile them with calendar, mail, notes, and private web pages. At the right time, the pendant gives a sourced reminder and can prepare—but never silently send—the follow-up.

2. **Honest 24 kHz audio path:** The current microphone captures at 15,625 Hz, so the system cannot truthfully call uplink audio superwideband. A production audio front end, explicit format negotiation, end-to-end sample-rate tests, and a verified 16 kHz fallback are needed.

What I still need is not another permission request. The important missing infrastructure is:

- A durable commitment/obligation ledger with provenance, due windows, deduplication, completion, and snooze states.
- Cross-surface reconciliation that can join a spoken commitment to calendar, mail, notes, and authenticated browser evidence without copying whole pages into prompts.
- A local interruption gate and delivery acknowledgement so reminders defer safely when the owner is busy, driving, offline, or already speaking.
- An approval-aware follow-up compiler producing previews, evidence, and receipts.
- A verified 24 kHz audio acceptance test plus CPU, RAM, LTE-M power, and playback measurements on the actual target wearable.

The Mac’s Accessibility/Screen Recording and browser-bridge grants remain owner-side blockers; I will not re-request them. The accessibility-free AppleScript, relay, pendant, and authenticated-read surfaces are sufficient to build the commitment loop’s first version.

args.user_asks: “When I leave home, work, or another place I choose, quietly check where I’m going next and tell me what I need to bring, finish, or remember before I get there.”
args.why_useful: A calendar reminder says where an appointment is; it does not notice that the owner is actually leaving, reconcile the destination with open work and private web tasks, or catch the one item left behind. The pendant can provide the moment-of-departure signal, the relay can remain available when the Mac sleeps, and the Mac/browser can assemble a short, evidence-backed departure checklist from calendar, mail, notes, and logged-in reservation or work pages. This is proactive physical-world context, not another scheduled briefing.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic geofence and calendar matching first. Use a cheaper background model to compose and rank the checklist. Reserve realtime only for ambiguous spoken corrections such as “I’m not going to the office after all.”
args.latency_budget: A departure event should produce a useful checklist within 5–15 seconds, with a local fallback such as “You have an appointment nearby.” Background page reconciliation may take up to two minutes and must never delay leaving.
args.cost_estimate: Usually below $0.01 per departure when calendar and cached context suffice; $0.02–$0.08 when authenticated browser extraction or synthesis is needed. GNSS checks and LTE-M bursts add battery cost, so use motion-triggered sampling and coarse geofences rather than continuous tracking.
args.security_concerns: Location history is highly sensitive. Keep exact coordinates on-device, send only a named place and coarse destination when possible, expire departure events quickly, and provide a hardware-button or voice disable mode. Browser/mail content must remain source-scoped and cited. Never send a message, alter a reservation, or buy anything from the checklist without explicit confirmation.
missing: Pendant-side GNSS/geofence and motion-trigger support, with coarse-place derivation that works during a dropped LTE link.
A privacy-preserving place profile store: named places, entry/exit rules, retention limits, and an owner-visible audit trail.
A destination resolver that joins place events to calendar and relevant open threads, then ranks only time-critical checklist items.
A local checklist cache and delivery acknowledgement so the pendant can speak a short fallback even when the Mac, browser bridge, or relay is unavailable.
built_from: POST /pipeline/events for departure and delivery provenance
POST /capture and GET /capture for owner corrections and one-off place notes
GET /machine-context and GET /context-graph for current destination and relevant entities
GET /briefing/latest and POST /briefing for the spoken checklist queue
POST /routines and POST /routines/:routineId/run for geofence-triggered reconciliation
GET /browser/sessions and the authenticated browser inspection/command-result routes for private reservation and work context
POST /execute and GET /jobs/:jobId/receipts for any explicitly approved follow-up action

args.change: Add a local departure-signal subsystem to the wearable: GNSS-capable location sampling with geofence evaluation and a low-power motion trigger, keeping exact coordinates in volatile/on-device storage and emitting only a named/coarse place-transition event upstream. Include a physical privacy-disable gesture and a bounded local checklist cache for disconnected operation.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can receive a timely, private “before you leave” checklist without carrying the phone or remembering to ask. It catches forgotten items and preparation steps at the only moment they are still fixable, while avoiding a permanent location trail in the cloud.
args.effort: High: select or enable GNSS on the nRF9160 design, characterize acquisition and LTE-M coexistence, implement geofence/motion firmware, privacy controls, encrypted local state, and relay event semantics. Product enclosure and antenna redesign may be required.
args.risk: GNSS can be slow indoors, inaccurate in cities, and power-hungry; false departures could annoy the owner. Use hysteresis, motion confirmation, named-place confidence, quiet hours, and a local disable latch. If GNSS is unavailable, fall back to owner-triggered place changes and never claim certainty.
args.cost_impact: Approximately $2–$10 incremental BOM if the modem/antenna can be reused, potentially more for RF and enclosure redesign. GNSS acquisition adds intermittent power draw and may increase LTE-M airtime only when a place transition is confirmed.
args.latency_impact: Cold fixes may take tens of seconds, so motion-triggered prediction and cached geofences should provide an immediate provisional event; final confirmation can arrive later. No impact on ordinary voice latency.
args.security_impact: Materially increases the sensitivity of the device. Exact coordinates must not leave the pendant by default; retain only coarse place IDs and short-lived transition records upstream. Privacy disable must be locally enforceable even with a compromised relay.
depends_on: A typed place-transition event contract shared by pendant, relay, Mac, and dashboard
A durable privacy policy for location retention and source disclosure
A local checklist cache and delivery acknowledgement protocol
A destination/context joiner that consumes the coarse event without requiring raw coordinates

A tactile contract would make the whole hive useful in meetings, transit, and noisy environments while keeping the Mac/browser work invisible to bystanders. args.risk: False or excessive taps could erode trust, and vibration may be uncomfortable or audible on hard surfaces. Bound daily notification volume, add quiet hours and a physical stop gesture, use escalating patterns sparingly, and retain a delivery/ack receipt for recovery after reconnect.

args.security_concerns: Battery, network, and queued-work metadata leave the pendant only to the authenticated relay/Mac; page contents and secrets must not be copied merely because a migration occurs. Require confirmation before migrating an irreversible action or sending anything; preserve owner-visible receipts and allow cancellation.
missing: Pendant battery/link telemetry exposed to the relay with hysteresis and last-known timestamp
A portable, resumable job checkpoint format with leases and deduplication across relay and Mac

args.why_useful_to_owner: A dying or disconnected pendant would stop being a cliff. The owner would hear only the few things that truly cannot wait, while ordinary research, briefings, and drafts finish elsewhere and are ready when the pendant returns.
args.effort: Medium-high: typed job schema and migrations, relay coordinator, pendant telemetry event, Mac handoff endpoint, reconnect reconciliation, failure-injection tests for power loss and duplicate execution.
args.risk: A stale battery reading could migrate too late or wake the Mac unnecessarily; use hysteresis, timestamps, conservative defaults, and leases. Duplicate work is contained by idempotency keys; unresolved jobs remain visibly pending rather than claiming success. Recovery is cancel/undo where supported plus a receipt explaining the boundary.
args.cost_impact: Small relay storage and polling overhead; occasional Mac wake/network traffic. No meaningful per-request model cost if urgency and thresholds are deterministic.
args.latency_impact: Adds seconds of checkpoint overhead only near a risk threshold; normal interactive requests unchanged. Reconnect recovery should be available within one health poll.
args.security_impact: Authenticated device-to-relay telemetry only; do not replicate private page contents unless the job already authorized it. Preserve per-surface provenance and require owner confirmation at irreversible checkpoints.

Pendant battery and link telemetry

args.change: Ship a negotiated 24-kHz superwideband Opus profile end to end: capture at the actual 15,625-Hz I2S rate, resample once with a fixed-point polyphase stage to 24 kHz, encode mono Opus at an explicit 24-kHz/24–32-kbps profile, and advertise that profile in the session handshake. Keep the existing 16-kHz/16-kbps mode as a fallback selected by measured CPU/packet-loss budget. On the relay, remove any implicit 16-kHz downsample, preserve the profile in queued audio jobs and receipts, and validate decoded sample rate/frame duration before delivery. On playback, retain the existing 24-kHz decode but replace the 31,250-Hz wire-clock assumption with a negotiated rate conversion contract so the ESP32's mandatory 44.1-kHz SBC path remains the only final resample. Add loopback fixtures for tones, speech, packet loss, and clock drift; reject a session rather than silently claiming 24 kHz when a stage falls back.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The pendant would sound intelligibly fuller and less muffled for both live replies and queued briefings, with no false promise that '24 kHz' survived the trip. Calls remain usable when bandwidth or battery is poor because fallback is explicit, not a broken half-upgrade.
args.effort: Medium-high: firmware resampler/profile and handshake, relay transcode/schema updates, ESP32 clock-contract update, and hardware-in-the-loop audio fixtures. The current implementation is a prototype and the owner explicitly asked to ship this path.
args.risk: A second resampler and higher Opus bitrate can increase CPU, latency, airtime, and dropouts; current hardware reports ~87% of one core when encode and decode both run. Mitigate by benchmarking encode-only/decode-only separately, selecting profile before streaming, bounded jitter buffers, and automatic fallback. Never silently mix 16-kHz and 24-kHz timestamps. Recovery is reconnect into the legacy profile.
args.cost_impact: No API-model cost change. Rough firmware/storage work fits existing flash but needs profiling; 24–32 kbps uses about 1.5–2x radio airtime versus 16 kbps, with corresponding modem energy increase. A production device may need a better audio codec/DSP if the nRF9160 cannot sustain duplex headroom.
args.latency_impact: Target unchanged 60-ms frames plus <=20 ms resampling; expect roughly 5–15 ms extra buffering during negotiation and possibly higher airtime latency. Keep live voice on the realtime tier; queued audio can use the cheaper background path.
args.security_impact: Audio remains encrypted in the existing authenticated session; profile metadata and loopback diagnostics should exclude raw speech by default. Store only hashes/metrics in receipts, apply short retention to generated audio, and require explicit opt-in before uploading diagnostic clips.

args.user_asks: “I’m leaving—pack up what I’m doing so I can continue from the pendant, and pick it back up when I return.”
args.why_useful: Today leaving the desk severs context: open Mac work, authenticated browser tabs, and half-finished plans are not converted into something usable while walking. args.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only to hear the short departure/return command and deliver the first acknowledgment. args.latency_budget: Acknowledge in under 1 second. Capture Mac/browser state in 5–15 seconds, produce a 30–90 second audio queue in under 60 seconds, and make the return workspace available as soon as the Mac reconnects. Offline pendant playback must not wait for the Mac.
args.cost_estimate: One small background summarization per handoff (roughly a few cents or less depending on transcript/page volume); realtime cost is limited to two short utterances. Dominant costs are private-page extraction and audio generation, not orchestration.
args.security_concerns: Snapshot only the active window, selected browser tabs, task text, and provenance—not arbitrary screenshots or full page bodies. Redact secrets and mark authenticated excerpts as private. Never send mail, submit forms, or alter files as part of packing. Returning may reopen sensitive tabs, so require a local button press or spoken confirmation if the snapshot contains private browser sessions. Expire the handoff after 24 hours and provide one-tap deletion.

A local pendant queue/marker that survives a dropped link and reports played/paused/expired state
A return-time revalidation step that checks tabs/files have not changed before reopening or continuing
Reliable browser bridge connectivity and explicit offline behavior (current home-chrome is offline with pending commands)
A compact audio renderer/acknowledgment path with the negotiated 24-kHz profile

args.risk: Adapters may disagree about identifiers or accidentally replay stale actions. Use immutable envelope IDs, source hashes, TTL, explicit 'changed' state, and default to read-only resume; destructive actions remain confirmation-gated. If one surface fails, preserve the envelope and deliver a partial handoff.
args.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; one compact background summary and optional audio render per envelope. Storage is small metadata plus references, not copied private pages or screenshots.
args.latency_impact: Packing adds roughly 1–3 seconds for metadata and 5–60 seconds for optional summary/audio. Return begins with a fast receipt lookup, then revalidation in background; no need to block spoken acknowledgment.
args.security_impact: Improves security by centralizing redaction, TTL, deletion, and provenance. Do not duplicate authenticated content into relay prompts; retain tab/file references and hashes, encrypt any audio, and log access without raw contents.

args.why_useful: People lose valuable social context because names, roles, promises, and personal details arrive while their hands are occupied. This gives the owner durable, privacy-respecting continuity without requiring note-taking during a conversation. It must distinguish observed facts from inference and let the owner correct or delete the card.
args.model_tier: Realtime handles only the explicit “remember this” marker and a short confirmation. args.latency_budget: A local acknowledgement under 1 second; a preliminary identity candidate within 10 seconds; enrichment and relationship-card construction can take minutes asynchronously. Before the next meeting, deliver a 15–30 second spoken card.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.02–$0.10 per saved conversation, dominated by transcription, entity resolution, and optional web enrichment. Most retrievals should be cached and text-only.
args.security_concerns: Conversation audio and relationship data are highly sensitive. Recording must require an explicit local gesture or spoken confirmation, with a visible/haptic recording indicator and an immediate cancel/delete control. Never record continuously by default, never infer sensitive traits, and never send a message or expose the card to another person without confirmation. Public enrichment must be source-labeled and limited to the identified person.

transcript.text:
I still need one foundational layer: a **cross-surface truth ledger**.

The live system currently has contradictory reports:

- `/ops/status`: Calendar and Mail automation are granted.
- `/briefing/latest`: says both need an Automation grant.
- `/browser/status`: Chrome is offline with 12 queued commands.
- `/pipeline`: contains completed runs alongside runs still marked `processing`.

I proposed:

1. **Truth Ledger and freshness gate** — claims carry source, timestamp, expiry, confidence, and sensitivity; contradictions are spoken as contradictions rather than silently resolved.
2. **Incident timeline and safe retry** — correlate pendant → relay → Mac → browser → audio receipts, explain where a request stalled, and preview retries without replaying potentially destructive actions.

What I still need is not another owner permission. I need the implementation to connect the existing routes—status, briefing, pipeline, browser, journal, jobs, and receipts—with:

- Stable correlation IDs across every surface.
- Explicit freshness and source-precedence rules.
- A pre-speech/pre-action contradiction check.
- Duplicate-risk detection before retries.
- Redacted, short spoken explanations for failures.

Until that exists, the system should conservatively say **“I have conflicting reports”** rather than claim that a task, permission, or delivery is complete.

args.user_asks: Before I commit to something, let me rehearse the consequences: check my calendar, current commitments, private messages, travel or account details, and active browser work; show what this choice would collide with, what it would make harder, and a few safe alternatives—without changing anything.
args.why_useful: The owner can ask the system to execute isolated tasks, but cannot yet ask it to reason about a life decision across all of the places where consequences are distributed. A rehearsal would prevent accidental overbooking, missed obligations, contradictory replies, and commitments made without seeing the relevant private context. It is advice and simulation, not autonomous action.
args.model_tier: Use a cheaper background reasoning model to gather and normalize facts and generate multiple scenarios; use the realtime tier only for the short spoken result and follow-up questions. Escalate to the expensive tier only when evidence conflicts or the decision has high stakes.
args.latency_budget: A quick rehearsal in 5 seconds from cached context; a thorough one in 20 seconds with fresh private-page checks. The pendant should give an immediate acknowledgement while the deeper analysis runs.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.05 per rehearsal, dominated by authenticated browser reads and synthesis rather than speech. Cache stable obligations and only refresh volatile sources.
args.security_concerns: Keep mail, calendar, account, and page contents on their owning surfaces; pass typed facts and redacted excerpts to the judge where possible. Clearly label inference versus evidence. No messages, bookings, edits, or submissions occur in rehearsal mode; any conversion to action requires a new confirmation and a fresh precondition check.
missing: A read-only scenario/rehearsal contract that takes a proposed commitment plus constraints and returns impacts, uncertainties, and alternatives.
A cross-surface obligation model that links calendar events, reminders, messages, browser transactions, travel details, and active work without copying sensitive payloads unnecessarily.
A temporal consequence engine for detecting collisions, deadlines, dependencies, and opportunity costs.
An explicit boundary in the action layer preventing rehearsal outputs from becoming queued mutations, plus provenance for every cited consequence.

args.change: Introduce a visibly separate `REHEARSE` conversation state spanning pendant, relay, Mac, and browser. In this state, all retrieved facts are assembled into an immutable scenario snapshot; the judge may branch alternatives and calculate consequences, but the action router is structurally unable to enqueue mutations. The owner can say `make this real` only after reviewing a compact delta that lists every proposed change, affected surface, evidence age, uncertainty, and duplicate risk; that phrase creates a new action plan rather than upgrading the rehearsal in place.
args.why_useful_to_owner: They can explore consequential choices while walking or away from the Mac without fear that asking 'what if?' will send a message, alter a calendar, replay a browser command, or spend a scarce approval. The owner gets understandable alternatives first and deliberate execution second.
args.effort: Medium-to-large: add a scenario snapshot and branch format to the relay protocol, propagate mode through planner and browser requests, enforce a deny-by-construction mutation guard, then add a review-to-action transition with fresh preconditions.
args.risk: A stale snapshot could produce an attractive but wrong rehearsal. Show observation times, mark unknowns, refresh volatile facts before conversion to action, and expire snapshots quickly. If mode metadata is lost, fail closed as read-only.
args.cost_impact: Small persistent metadata and one additional synthesis call when branching alternatives; no mutation or browser-action cost during rehearsal. Realtime speech remains limited to acknowledgement and summary.
args.latency_impact: Immediate local acknowledgement; 5–20 seconds for scenario assembly depending on private-source refreshes. Conversion adds a final precondition check.
args.security_impact: Strongly reduces accidental side effects and prevents scenario text from being mistaken for executable intent. Sensitive evidence remains source-local and only redacted claims enter the scenario snapshot.
depends_on: A cross-surface typed fact/obligation projection
Stable provenance and freshness metadata
A mutation-deny guard enforced below the planner, not merely in prompts
Existing job, browser, pipeline, and receipt identifiers

args.user_asks: Keep my pendant’s speech clear automatically as I move between a quiet room, a noisy street, and a Mac/browser call—without making me run a calibration each time.
args.why_useful: The owner gets consistent intelligibility during the moments they actually rely on the pendant. A tiny device can sense acoustic conditions, the relay can choose a safe low-latency profile, and the Mac/browser can apply the matching input/output route; each change is reversible and reported in one short receipt.
args.model_tier: Use a deterministic/on-device classifier and cheap relay DSP scorer for routine environment changes; reserve realtime model only for ambiguous transitions or when the owner asks why audio changed. No background LLM call is needed for ordinary profile switches.
args.latency_budget: Classify locally in under 100 ms; relay decision and profile push under 300 ms; Mac/browser application under 1 s. Never interrupt speech for a profile change; queue it until an utterance boundary.
args.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.001 per transition (telemetry plus deterministic DSP); occasional explanation costs one realtime turn. Storage is a few hundred bytes per transition plus profile definitions.
args.security_concerns: Transmit features/levels, not raw room audio, by default; discard any calibration snippets immediately after scoring. Call apps and browser tab identity are sensitive, so expose only the selected route/profile in receipts. Require confirmation before changing a call’s active microphone or camera; volume/EQ and reversible device selection may follow the owner’s existing automation policy.

a relay profile state machine with hysteresis, utterance-boundary application, rollback, and durable receipts;
Mac/browser adapters that can apply and verify profiles through the existing granted AppleScript/high-level actions, plus a dashboard timeline of profile changes;
acceptance tests for 24 kHz speech intelligibility, transition latency, clipping, and privacy deletion.

args.change: Add an event-boundary audio adaptation service: compute 10 Hz bands/level/noise-floor/clipping features locally, classify quiet/voice-noise/music/wind with hysteresis, and publish only a signed profile recommendation (not raw audio) over the existing audio/events path. args.why_useful_to_owner: Speech remains understandable without the owner fiddling with settings, while a long press gives them an immediate, dependable way to stop automation in a sensitive environment.
args.effort: Medium firmware work plus relay contract and Mac/browser adapters; 2–3 weeks including acoustic acceptance tests.
args.risk: A wrong classifier could make audio worse or change during a call. Hysteresis, confidence thresholds, utterance-boundary application, profile rollback, and a freeze gesture recover safely; default profile remains unchanged on link loss.
args.cost_impact: No meaningful API cost; roughly 8–16 KB code, under 6 KB RAM, and negligible flash writes if recommendations are rate-limited. Hardware cost $0 on prototype.
args.latency_impact: Feature windows add 100 ms; profile changes take effect within 1 s but never mid-utterance.
args.security_impact: Only coarse acoustic features and signed recommendations leave the pendant; no raw room audio is retained. Freeze gesture is local and works offline.

args.user_asks: If the pendant or relay is unsure what I said, catch the bad phrase before anything happens, ask me for only that phrase, and then continue the original request without making me start over.
args.why_useful: Today a noisy or clipped word can turn a perfectly good spoken request into a failed action or, worse, the wrong action. The owner should experience a two-second, targeted repair instead of repeating an entire multi-step thought or discovering the mistake afterward.
args.model_tier: Use streaming ASR confidence, acoustic clipping features, and deterministic entity/action validation first. Invoke the realtime model only to formulate the shortest repair question and reconcile the corrected span; use a cheaper background model for post-action quality analytics.
args.latency_budget: Detect a suspect span within 250 ms of the utterance end and ask within 700 ms. Preserve the original intent for up to 30 seconds while waiting; never block unrelated audio or silently guess after the repair window expires.
args.cost_estimate: Routine turns add negligible DSP/metadata cost; roughly one extra realtime turn only when a repair is needed, typically <$0.01 per repair. Keep only the original and corrected transcript spans plus hashes, not raw audio.
args.security_concerns: The system must not execute an irreversible action while any required slot is uncertain. Show the owner the exact disputed word/field on the Mac when available, speak no sensitive surrounding transcript aloud in public, and expire the pending intent locally and server-side after 30 seconds. Confirmation remains mandatory for sending, deleting, purchasing, or other destructive actions.
missing: A typed utterance-repair protocol carrying span offsets, confidence, acoustic-failure reason, preserved intent, expiry, and corrected value across pendant and relay
A deterministic pre-action validator that marks which slots are safety-critical and refuses to fill them by best guess
A low-memory pendant clipping/noise feature stream and a local retry tone/button path that works through a dropped link
A faculty-action transaction hold that can resume the same plan after one corrected span, with a receipt showing original, repair, and final values
Mac/browser UI support for highlighting the disputed field without replaying the entire request

args.change: Introduce a first-class 'uncertain span' transaction state between perception and action. The planner must carry the original intent and all resolved slots, mark only low-confidence spans, ask one targeted spoken repair, then re-run validation and produce a diff before releasing the action. If the link drops, the pendant stores a compact repair token and gives a local retry tone; it never guesses or expires into execution.
args.why_useful_to_owner: A clipped name, number, or date no longer forces the owner to repeat an entire request or risk the wrong real-world action. They get a fast, understandable repair and continuity across the pendant, relay, Mac, and browser.
args.effort: Medium protocol and UX work across perception/action/relay plus a small firmware queue; extensive adversarial tests for stale repairs, duplicate delivery, and destructive actions.
args.risk: A stale correction could be attached to the wrong request, or repeated prompts could annoy the owner. Bind every repair to an intent hash, tab/job/session ID, and short expiry; cap retries at one and fall back to a clear failure receipt.
args.cost_impact: Minimal persistent storage (under 1 KB per pending repair); one additional realtime turn only on uncertain speech; no new hardware required.
args.latency_impact: Adds under 700 ms when repair is needed; zero added latency to high-confidence utterances.
args.security_impact: This is a safety barrier: uncertain destructive fields cannot pass. Sensitive transcript spans remain encrypted and expire; only the disputed span is spoken or displayed.

args.change: Replace the prototype's implicit audio assumptions with an explicit negotiated profile and loopback contract: pendant advertises capture/playback rates, frame duration, Opus mode, battery/thermal headroom, and firmware version; relay selects a profile, stamps every segment with profile+sequence+CRC, and runs a nightly fixture test that compares a 24 kHz source through uplink/transcode/decode/I2S output. args.user_asks: Keep me aware of genuinely urgent changes without making me pull out my phone or broadcasting private information in public; use a private signal now and explain it later.
args.why_useful: Today the system can speak, queue jobs, and inspect surfaces, but it cannot reliably arbitrate urgency across calendar/mail/browser/Mac signals and deliver a discreet, offline-tolerant signal on the wearable. This would let the owner stay reachable during a commute, meeting, or hands-busy moment without turning every notification into an interruption.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic rules and a cheap background model to classify urgency and deduplicate events; reserve realtime for the owner's follow-up question. Never spend the expensive conversational tier merely to decide that an unchanged notification is nonurgent.
args.latency_budget: Urgent events should reach the relay within 5 seconds and the pendant within 2 seconds of connectivity. If disconnected, latch the signal locally and deliver the explanation when the link returns; nonurgent items can wait for the next briefing.
args.cost_estimate: Usually <$0.005 per event batch; the dominant cost is occasional model classification of ambiguous messages. Haptic delivery and event metadata are negligible.
args.security_concerns: Urgency classification must minimize content exposure: prefer sender, deadline, and user-defined domains before message bodies. Keep private signals content-free, encrypt event metadata, expire raw excerpts, and require confirmation for any resulting external action. The owner must be able to define people, topics, and quiet hours, with an unmistakable physical all-clear/stop control.
missing: A pendant actuator and firmware protocol for at least three private urgency patterns plus a local latch that survives a dropped link and reboot.
A shared event-ingestion and deduplication stream from Mac notifications, Calendar, Mail, and authenticated browser watches, with source, deadline, confidence, and expiry.
A policy engine that combines urgency, quiet hours, current activity, and repetition history without silently escalating low-confidence events.
A delivery receipt and later explanation view that proves why the signal fired, what evidence supported it, and whether it was acknowledged.

args.change: Add a low-power haptic actuator with a dedicated interrupt-capable driver and a small nonvolatile attention latch (plus a physical acknowledge/stop input) to the wearable. Define three patterns—urgent, time-sensitive, and informational—whose waveform carries no message content; the relay sends only a signed event class and expiry, while the pendant can signal urgent events during a link outage and report acknowledgement after reconnect.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can receive a private, glance-free warning in public or while hands are occupied, without a speaker announcing sensitive content and without losing an important event just because Wi-Fi or the Mac went to sleep.
args.effort: Hardware revision plus firmware driver, battery characterization, enclosure/acoustic isolation tests, relay event signing, and a small user calibration flow. This deliberately adds a capability rather than pretending the current single-LED/button prototype can provide reliable private urgency levels.
args.risk: False alarms could erode trust; missed alarms could be serious. Start with advisory notifications, require explicit owner-selected sources, expose a physical universal stop, expire stale latches, and log every trigger/acknowledgement for review. Haptic vibration can affect battery life and comfort.
args.cost_impact: Rough prototype addition: approximately $2–$8 for actuator, driver, and passives, plus PCB/enclosure changes; brief pulses likely add tens of milliwatts while active, with negligible average draw at low event rates. No model cost for delivery.
args.latency_impact: Local haptic onset can be under 100 ms after a signed event arrives; event arbitration and Mac/browser ingestion remain network-bound.
args.security_impact: The pendant receives only an authenticated class, expiry, and event identifier—not message text. Protect the latch against spoofing and ensure a stolen pendant cannot reveal private content through pattern semantics beyond the owner-configured vocabulary.
depends_on: A cross-surface urgency/deduplication policy and event stream
Owner-configured quiet hours, source allowlist, and confidence threshold
Delivery receipt and explanation records for every haptic event

transcript.text:

- A cross-surface **private urgency channel** that filters calendar, mail, browser, and Mac events, then discreetly signals only genuinely urgent items on the wearable and explains them later.
- A hardware/firmware change adding a **low-power haptic actuator**, signed urgency patterns, offline latching, acknowledgement, expiry, and a physical stop control.

These require a shared event stream, urgency/deduplication policy, owner-configured quiet hours and source allowlists, delivery receipts, and a pendant hardware revision.

args.user_asks: “Make spoken replies and my queued briefings sound clear, but never let them stutter: use 24 kHz when the link and pendant can sustain it, fall back smoothly when they cannot, and resume at the exact sentence if I walk out of coverage.”
args.why_useful: The current pendant path can decode 24 kHz playback but capture/uplink is 16 kHz, and simultaneous Opus encode/decode consumes roughly 87% of one Cortex-M33 core. A fixed mode will either waste quality or cause glitches. A hive-level adaptive session would let the owner hear consistently intelligible speech, preserve queued work through connectivity loss, and avoid replaying a briefing from the beginning.
args.model_tier: Use the realtime tier only for the live conversational turn and codec-mode negotiation; use a cheaper background worker for transcoding, queue preparation, and sentence-boundary indexing.
args.latency_budget: Mode negotiation under 300 ms at session start; fallback within 1–2 lost frames (120 ms) with a short crossfade; queued-briefing recovery can take seconds and must not block live speech.
args.cost_estimate: Small incremental API cost: mostly background Opus transcode/storage already paid for; roughly one extra cheap worker invocation per queued item, with bandwidth/storage dominating. Realtime token cost is unchanged if negotiation is structured metadata rather than prose.
args.security_concerns: Audio remains private and should stay in the existing authenticated relay storage. Telemetry should contain only codec mode, packet loss, battery/thermal buckets, and sentence IDs—not transcript text. Switching mode is reversible and needs no confirmation; deleting or pinning recordings still follows the owner's retention policy.
missing: A firmware capability/telemetry handshake exposing supported playback modes, decoder CPU headroom, queue cursor, and a local sentence-boundary resume marker.
Relay-side adaptive jitter buffer and Opus profile switch with sequence continuity and crossfade, rather than starting a new unrelated stream.
A background audio compiler that emits sentence/word boundary indexes and low/high-fidelity variants, plus garbage-collectable retention metadata.
Mac-side preflight and fallback notification so a briefing can be prepared or surfaced locally when the pendant is offline.
An end-to-end fault-injection test covering loss, reconnect, duplicate packets, SD failure buffer, and resume without duplicate speech.

args.change: Add an audio-session capability handshake and resumable playback cursor to the pendant protocol: advertise supported Opus rates/frame sizes, report coarse CPU/battery/link buckets, accept a mode switch only at a packet boundary, persist the current sentence ID plus sequence number in a tiny journal, and expose an explicit reconnect/resume event. Pair this with relay-side mode arbitration and a Mac preflight that selects 24 kHz, 16 kHz, or a pre-rendered fallback before delivery.
args.why_useful_to_owner: Briefings and replies would remain understandable instead of glitching or restarting when the owner moves between coverage or the pendant is busy. The owner gets one continuous conversation and can resume a long briefing where they stopped.
args.effort: Medium-high: protocol versioning, nRF9160 Opus scheduling, relay jitter/transcode state, Mac preflight, and network fault-injection tests across the four surfaces.
args.risk: A bad mode switch could produce silence, duplicated speech, or an unrecoverable cursor. Mitigate with capability-version negotiation, boundary-only switches, a watchdog fallback to the known 16 kHz path, journal checksum, and server-side duplicate suppression. Roll back by disabling negotiation and using the current fixed profile.
args.cost_impact: Negligible model cost; modest relay CPU for dual-variant transcode and temporary boundary metadata. Firmware flash/RAM impact should stay small (roughly 8–16 kB flash and under 4 kB RAM if the journal is compact).
args.latency_impact: Adds under 300 ms at session setup; recovery adds at most one short buffered segment. Normal speech should not gain a model round trip.
args.security_impact: Only coarse device telemetry and opaque sentence/sequence IDs leave the pendant; no transcript is added. Resume journals on SD must obey the existing rule that SD is a failure buffer, with bounded expiry and encryption if it contains audio references.
depends_on: A versioned audio control message path between pendant, ESP32 bridge, and relay
Relay adaptive jitter/transcode state and sentence-boundary indexing
A Mac offline/preflight hook
End-to-end audio loss/reconnect tests

args.user_asks: “Erase everything this hive knows about [topic/person/project] everywhere, prove what was erased, and stop any queued or offline action that depends on it.”
args.why_useful: Today a private fact or sensitive project can be distributed across relay job records, generated audio, Mac workspace files, browser-session state, pending commands, receipts, and the pendant’s failure buffer. The owner has no single, verifiable way to revoke that knowledge across all bodies. A topic-scoped cryptographic erasure and revocation operation would provide a real safety boundary, not merely a promise that future prompts will omit it.
args.model_tier: Use a deterministic background control-plane worker for indexing, revocation, deletion, and verification; use the realtime tier only to clarify the topic scope and speak the final receipt.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge the request immediately; revoke queued work within 2 seconds; complete online erasure and produce a receipt within 30 seconds. Offline pendant and Mac components must apply the tombstone on reconnect before accepting work.
args.cost_estimate: Low model cost and modest control-plane/API cost. The dominant cost is enumerating and verifying distributed stores; no transcript generation is needed.
args.security_concerns: The erase request itself must not echo the secret in logs or spoken output. Use a keyed topic fingerprint, per-surface deletion capability, authenticated tombstones, and append-only proof metadata that records locations and outcomes without retaining content. Destructive erasure requires explicit confirmation, except for a separately configured physical panic gesture. The system must distinguish successful deletion, inaccessible storage, and cryptographic invalidation, never claim complete erasure when a surface is offline.
missing: A hive-wide data inventory that maps each artifact, pending action, browser session value, audio object, file, and device journal to privacy-scope fingerprints without copying sensitive content.
A signed, monotonic revocation/tombstone protocol consumed by relay, Mac, browser bridge, and pendant offline queue before execution or replay.
Per-surface secure deletion adapters: R2/D1 and logs on relay; workspace/receipt/job artifacts on Mac; browser extension/session caches; pendant SD failure-buffer records and local journals.
A verification sweep that returns a surface-by-surface receipt and retries or escalates offline failures, with an owner-visible distinction between erased and merely revoked.
A policy preventing model context, scheduled routines, and queued jobs from rehydrating a revoked scope.

args.change: Replace the prototype pendant’s single momentary button with a dedicated, latching privacy control that electrically disconnects the I2S microphone and signals the state with a hard-to-misread physical indicator. Add a small secure element or protected flash region for a device identity and an erase/revocation counter, so the pendant can reject stale queued commands after a privacy event even while offline. Firmware must treat the switch as authoritative, zeroize volatile audio buffers, stop capture, and emit only a minimal privacy-state event on reconnect.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner could put the pendant on a table in a confidential meeting and know—without trusting software, network state, or a model—that it cannot hear them. After privacy is lifted, old offline work cannot silently replay against the new context.
args.effort: High hardware revision plus firmware and relay protocol changes: microphone power/clock gating, debounce and boot-state handling, secure-counter integration, enclosure redesign, and certification/regression testing.
args.risk: A stuck or bounced switch could disable conversations or create a false sense of privacy. Use a mechanically stable two-position control, visible state, boot self-test, and an explicit spoken/LED confirmation when capture resumes. Treat any hardware fault as privacy-on. Secure-counter failure must fail closed and allow recovery only through a local owner procedure.
args.cost_impact: Prototype BOM increase roughly $2–6 for a latching switch, mic power gate, indicator, and secure element, plus board/enclosure NRE; negligible ongoing API cost and sub-milliwatt standby impact.
args.latency_impact: Privacy engagement is immediate; resume adds under 500 ms for hardware settle and session renegotiation.
args.security_impact: Strongly improves the trust boundary by making microphone disablement independent of the application and relay. The device identity/counter prevents replay of pre-privacy commands, but it introduces key provisioning and replacement/recovery obligations.
depends_on: A revised pendant PCB and enclosure (the current nRF9160 development kit has only a provisional single-button design)
Firmware capture pipeline that can zeroize buffers and persist a monotonic privacy epoch
Relay and Mac/browser queues that enforce the privacy epoch before execution
Owner-visible privacy-state receipts that do not include sensitive audio

args.user_asks: “Keep the pendant useful all day: spend battery and bandwidth on urgent things, defer or compress everything else, and tell me what was deferred before it becomes stale.”
args.why_useful: Today the hive has no owner-facing energy contract. A long briefing, live conversation, queued browser job, and urgent interruption compete blindly for the same pendant radio, CPU, and failure-buffer space. The owner should get graceful degradation rather than a dead device or silently lost work: urgent contact remains available, routine work is deferred with an expiry, and the Mac/relay can carry on when the pendant cannot.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic policy and a cheap background worker for energy prediction, queue reprioritization, and transcoding. Invoke the realtime tier only for an active conversation or a truly urgent spoken alert.
args.latency_budget: Urgency classification and budget update under 1 second; routine deferral is immediate. The Mac or relay may continue background work without pendant availability, while urgent delivery retries within 2 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: Low model/API cost because the decision is policy over device telemetry; occasional background summarization/transcoding dominates. It can reduce cost by avoiding unnecessary high-fidelity streaming and repeated retries.
args.security_concerns: Battery, link, and queue telemetry should be coarse and authenticated. Never silently discard owner work: every deferral needs an expiry and receipt. Urgency rules must be owner-configurable, with conservative defaults and an emergency override that may require confirmation for noisy alerts.
missing: A signed low-rate device telemetry stream for battery, radio quality, thermal/CPU headroom, SD capacity, and charging state.
A shared resource ledger that assigns budgets to live audio, queued briefings, browser/Mac jobs, and retry buffers with explicit expiry semantics.
Relay/Mac ability to continue and later reconcile work while the pendant is unavailable, without duplicating spoken output.
A policy evaluator that can distinguish urgent owner-defined events from routine work and explain each defer/compress decision.
A compact pendant status interaction so the owner can inspect or override the current budget without opening a screen.

transcript.text:
Recorded two proposals:

1. **Hive-wide topic erasure and revocation** — erase or cryptographically invalidate sensitive information across relay, Mac, browser, pendant buffers, queued jobs, and model context, with an honest surface-by-surface receipt.

2. **Energy-aware continuity** — keep urgent communication available while battery, bandwidth, CPU, or storage are constrained; defer, compress, or reroute routine work with expiry and an explanation rather than silently losing it.

Both require new cross-surface control-plane, telemetry, policy, and verification work rather than another isolated feature.

args.user_asks: “Handle it quietly, and only get my attention if you need me.”
args.why_useful: The owner can delegate routine Mac/browser work in public or during a conversation without the pendant reading private details aloud. The Mac and authenticated browser carry out reversible steps, the relay aggregates receipts, and the pendant gives a discreet completion/approval-needed signal; only an exception opens a spoken conversation.
args.model_tier: Use the slower background model for planning and receipt summarization; use realtime only if the owner presses the pendant after an approval-needed haptic or asks a follow-up.
args.latency_budget: Start acknowledgment within 1 second as a short haptic pattern; background work may take minutes. Exception escalation should be delivered within 10 seconds of a blocked step or bridge loss.
args.cost_estimate: Usually one cheap planning/receipt pass (roughly $0.01–$0.05 depending on task); no realtime tokens unless the owner engages. Hardware prototype cost roughly $3–$8 per unit for a coin ERM/LRA motor and $1–$3 for a fuel-gauge/ambient sensor if added.
args.security_concerns: Never expose message subjects, account names, or page contents through audio or LED patterns. Bind haptic outcomes to a job ID and approval token, expire them, and require a button press to authorize irreversible steps. Persist only redacted receipt metadata; keep sensitive browser data on the Mac/bridge.
missing: A pendant haptic actuator and driver (the current board has only one LED and one button)
A privacy mode in the relay/pipeline that routes status to haptics and suppresses speech
Typed cross-surface event/receipt contracts connecting Mac and browser jobs to a pendant notification queue
A user-visible mapping and cancellation gesture for haptic patterns

args.change: Add a low-power LRA haptic actuator with a DRV2605-class I2C driver, plus a battery fuel gauge and (optionally) an ambient-light/proximity sensor. Reserve three local patterns: short pulse = completed, double pulse = approval needed, long pulse = blocked/connection lost. Keep the existing button as cancel/acknowledge and the LED as a secondary diagnostic channel.
args.why_useful_to_owner: They can receive private, actionable status while in public, driving, or talking to someone, instead of hearing account names and task details aloud or missing an important blocked action. Battery-aware escalation can also avoid silently draining the wearable.
args.effort: Prototype wiring is modest because I2C is explicitly free; add board support, haptic patterns, event acknowledgements, enclosure and power tests. Product revision needs mechanical/acoustic validation and accessibility testing.
args.risk: Extra current draw and mechanical buzz could annoy the wearer; a bad pattern could be mistaken for an approval. Default to conservative patterns, allow disabling, require an explicit button press for approval, and fall back to LED/audio when the haptic self-test fails.
args.cost_impact: Approximately $4–$12 BOM increase (motor, driver, gauge, passives, sensor) and a few mA during pulses; no per-call API cost. Fuel gauge reduces uncertainty but adds always-on quiescent current.
args.latency_impact: Local acknowledgment is sub-100 ms once an event reaches the pendant; no model latency. Haptic queue must survive LTE reconnects without replaying expired events.
args.security_impact: Improves privacy by removing sensitive audio from routine status. Do not encode semantic content in patterns beyond urgency/state; encrypt and authenticate event IDs, and expire approval challenges.
depends_on: A typed relay-to-pendant notification event and acknowledgement protocol
Privacy-mode routing in the pipeline
Cross-surface job receipts with idempotent event IDs and expiry

args.change: Implement a durable Quiet-Intent channel: when the owner says 'quietly', unified issues a signed mode lease (scope, expiry, allowed surfaces, speech suppression) to relay; Mac and browser jobs publish typed lifecycle events; relay reduces them to redacted state changes and delivers exactly-once pendant notifications. A button press acknowledges or cancels the lease; bridge reconnects must not replay expired events. Approval-required events carry only a nonce and human-safe label, with full details retrieved after an intentional spoken interaction.
args.why_useful_to_owner: This turns 'quietly' into a dependable behavior rather than a best-effort promise: private work continues across the Mac, logged-in browser, and sleeping relay, while the wearer gets only the minimum signal needed to act and can recover from a lost connection without duplicate actions.
args.effort: Medium: define event and lease schemas, add relay D1 tables/TTL, adapt job/browser receipts, add reconnect reconciliation and tests for duplicate/out-of-order events, then add one voice command and dashboard history.
args.risk: A stale lease could suppress speech when the owner expects it, or a lost event could hide a blocked task. Leases must expire quickly, surface a visible current-mode indicator in the dashboard, and default to normal speech after expiry; every event remains queryable in receipts.
args.cost_impact: Negligible storage and relay compute; roughly $0.001–$0.01 per background event batch, with no realtime model call. Context cost drops because only redacted state is injected into voice turns.
args.latency_impact: Local mode acknowledgment under 1 s; event delivery normally under 2 s, with reconnect reconciliation on next heartbeat. No added model round trip for ordinary completions.
args.security_impact: Strong privacy gain: browser content never crosses into the haptic/status payload. Signed leases prevent a tab or stale job from changing speech policy; enforce owner-scoped authorization and redact labels.
depends_on: Cross-surface transaction coordinator from faculty-action
Durable browser job runner and typed receipts
A pendant notification/acknowledgement transport
Owner interruption and quiet-hours policy
