transcript.text:
Recorded three capabilities:

1. **Wear-presence privacy lock** — setting down the pendant locks private Mac/browser sessions and silences sensitive audio; reattachment restores context after authentication.
2. **Bounded private “mark that” capture** — saves only a short local audio clip, then lets the owner explicitly keep, transcribe, or erase it.
3. **High-confidence departure checklist** — combines calendar, routines, and local context to remind the owner about likely forgotten items without noisy interruptions.

Each requires new firmware, relay, and cross-surface coordination beyond today’s wiring.

result.note: These are the Mac agent routes. Your own backend may differ — probe_http hits whichever backend you run against.

result.link: LTE-M (Cat-M1) via the nRF9160 modem. Half duplex in practice.
result.transport: One TLS WebSocket to the Cloudflare Worker carries uplink and downlink audio simultaneously. Modem TLS record limit is about 2 kB.
result.measured: Uplink 16 kbps + downlink 24 kbps saturates the link under contention: a recent call dropped 388 uplink packets (~7.8 s of speech) when the agent was speaking at the same time the owner was.
result.status: PROTOTYPE. This is a Nordic development kit, not the product. Every choice here — the SoC, the RAM, the single button, the single LED, the enclosure — is provisional and can change. Design the device the owner should wear, then say what it would take to build it.
result.you_are_here: You run on the owner's MacBook (faculty-judgement). Every device described here is REMOTE to you — you are not running on the pendant or the ESP32.

args.user_asks: “Run my monthly access-resilience check: verify that my important accounts, backups, browser sessions, Mac, and pendant can still be recovered, and tell me exactly what would fail—without exposing any secrets or changing anything.”
args.why_useful: People discover a dead password, expired session, missing backup, or disconnected wearable only during a crisis. This turns recovery from an assumption into a private, non-destructive drill spanning the browser's logged-in sessions, Mac's local backup/configuration state, relay reachability, and the pendant's USB/offline path.
args.model_tier: Background model for monthly checks and evidence summarization; realtime only if the owner asks from the pendant.
args.latency_budget: A monthly run may take 2–5 minutes; spoken result under 30 seconds, with a detailed report on Mac.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.05–$0.25 per run depending on number of accounts/pages; browser and Mac inspection dominate, not generation.
args.security_concerns: Never read or persist passwords, recovery codes, message contents, or secret values; return boolean/age/health evidence only. Require confirmation for any offered repair. Encrypt the report and expire it quickly.
missing: A redacted account-recovery check protocol (health assertions rather than credential extraction)
Mac backup and keychain-presence inspectors that do not reveal values
A pendant USB/LTE connectivity self-test and a signed drill report
A monthly routine that can fan out across browser, Mac, and relay

So this is connective work rather than a new capability — say what is missing BETWEEN them, or whether it is already reachable today and nobody has wired it up.

args.change: Build a redacted cross-surface recovery drill: a monthly routine fans out health assertions to the browser bridge, Mac agent, relay, and USB-connected pendant, signs each result with timestamp/device identity, stores only pass/fail plus remediation class, and produces a human-readable failure map. Add synthetic test accounts/pages and a pendant loopback challenge so the drill proves the path rather than merely checking process liveness.
args.why_useful_to_owner: They learn before an emergency whether the thing they rely on can actually recover, without handing the system their passwords or dumping private content into a report.
args.effort: Medium-high: new assertions and a test harness on four surfaces, plus a small redacted report UI.
args.risk: A false green check could create dangerous confidence; every assertion needs a known limitation and periodic synthetic canary. A failed drill must not mutate accounts or trigger notifications.
args.cost_impact: <$0.10 monthly in model/API cost; engineering/storage cost is the main impact.
args.latency_impact: Runs in background; report generation under a minute after checks complete.
args.security_impact: Improves security by proving recovery while minimizing data. Requires strict no-secret logging, encrypted short-retention results, and owner-only access.
depends_on: A cross-surface health-assertion schema
Pendant loopback/self-test over its live USB serial connection
Browser and Mac inspectors that return metadata/booleans, never secret values

args.user_asks: “Audit my privacy across the pendant, relay, Mac, and logged-in browser: show me what sensitive material is stored where, who can reach it, and give me a safe, reversible cleanup plan.”
args.why_useful: The owner currently has to trust that audio, browser extracts, logs, drafts, and local files disappear when expected. A single, source-cited map makes invisible retention visible and lets them reduce exposure without manually hunting four systems.
args.model_tier: Background model for inventory, classification, and report writing; use realtime only when the owner asks for an immediate scan from the pendant.
args.latency_budget: 5–10 minutes for a full scan; a short spoken summary in under 20 seconds, with cleanup requiring explicit approval per category.
args.cost_estimate: $0.10–$0.50 per scan; classification of snippets and file metadata dominates. Keep raw content local where possible.
args.security_concerns: The audit itself is highly sensitive. Classify locally on Mac when possible, send hashes/locations rather than contents, redact secrets before relay storage, and require confirmation before deletion. Never scan or reveal unrelated third-party data.
missing: A unified retention inventory spanning relay objects, D1 pointers, Mac logs/files, browser inspection caches, and pendant flash
Local secret/PII classification with redacted counts and hashes
Preview/undo cleanup transactions across surfaces
A report UI that explains access boundaries and expiration dates

args.user_asks: “When I tap the pendant at the start and end of a conversation, securely capture that interval, transcribe it on my Mac, and leave me a private summary of decisions, names, and follow-ups—never record outside the two taps.”
args.why_useful: People lose the details that matter in conversations. A deliberate two-tap boundary gives the owner a reliable memory aid without an always-on recorder: the pendant supplies an unmistakable physical consent boundary, the bridge carries audio, and the Mac creates searchable notes and follow-ups.
args.model_tier: Local Mac speech-to-text and a cheaper background summarizer; realtime is unnecessary except to acknowledge the tap boundary.
args.latency_budget: Tap acknowledgement under 300 ms; transcript within 1 minute of ending; summary within 2 minutes.
args.cost_estimate: $0.02–$0.15 per conversation depending on local versus hosted transcription; audio transfer/storage dominates. Local transcription can make API cost near zero.
args.security_concerns: Require a physical start and stop tap, show a visible LED/audio cue, keep raw audio on the Mac by default with short retention, and warn about local recording-consent laws. Never upload or share without a separate confirmation. Provide an immediate stop/erase gesture.
missing: Pendant firmware start/stop recording state and unmistakable LED/audio cues
ESP32-to-Mac lossless interval capture with timestamps and drop detection
Local transcription plus speaker/decision extraction
A private notes destination and retention/erase controls

args.change: Add a physically bounded conversation-capture state machine to the pendant: double-press starts, double-press ends, long-press aborts and erases the current buffer; LED patterns and a short haptic/audio cue confirm each transition. Persist only an encrypted ring-buffer session id and byte count locally, and emit start/stop/drop events over USB serial so the Mac can reject incomplete recordings.
args.why_useful_to_owner: They can deliberately remember a real conversation without an always-on microphone, and they get an immediate, trustworthy signal that recording is or is not active.
args.effort: Medium: button debounce/state machine, cues, encrypted metadata, UART events, and serial test coverage.
args.risk: Accidental capture or missed stop; mitigate with unmistakable cues, a hard maximum duration, automatic expiry, and long-press erase. Hardware audio path currently has packet-loss risk under duplex contention.
args.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; under ~10 KB firmware storage and a few KB RAM, no new hardware. Audio transport may increase Mac/bridge bandwidth use.
args.latency_impact: Tap acknowledgement should be local under 300 ms; no network dependency.
args.security_impact: Improves consent and privacy by making capture opt-in and locally abortable; does not itself guarantee legal consent from other participants.
depends_on: Owner-approved recording policy and retention defaults

transcript.text:
This round produced four new directions:

1. **Tap-bounded conversation memory — the most immediately useful**
   - Double-tap the pendant to start and stop a recording; long-press erases it.
   - Mac transcribes and summarizes decisions, names, and follow-ups locally.
   - No always-on recording, with LED/audio confirmation and short retention.

2. **Monthly access-resilience drill**
   - Verify that important browser sessions, Mac backups, relay connectivity, and the pendant’s USB/LTE path can actually recover.
   - Report only redacted pass/fail evidence—never passwords or recovery codes.
   - This is especially important because the wearable is currently testable over USB but is not LTE-registered.

3. **Cross-device privacy audit**
   - Show where sensitive audio, browser extracts, logs, drafts, and files are retained across the pendant, Mac, browser, and relay.
   - Generate a reversible cleanup plan, with deletion requiring confirmation.

4. **Firmware support for deliberate recording**
   - Local double-press state machine, hard duration limit, abort-and-erase gesture, unmistakable cues, and UART start/stop/drop events.
   - Audio should buffer locally on the Mac rather than depend on the unreliable duplex LTE path.

What I still need is not another permission request. The practical blockers are:

- Pendant firmware support for local capture boundaries and cues.
- ESP32-to-Mac timestamping and packet-drop detection.
- Local Mac transcription and encrypted short-lived note storage.
- Redacted health assertions for account, backup, browser, relay, and device recovery.
- A unified retention inventory and reversible cleanup transaction across all surfaces.
- The owner’s explicit policy for recording conversations, including regional consent requirements.

A key hardware finding was confirmed: simultaneous 16 kbps uplink and 24 kbps downlink recently lost about 7.8 seconds of speech. Conversation capture must therefore be USB/Mac-first, not live LTE streaming.

transcript.text:
Round 138 produced:

- **Physical approval for consequential actions:** the Mac/browser prepares a precise diff, the pendant flashes a challenge, and one physical button press authorizes exactly that action. Stale or changed actions are rejected.
- **Decision provenance recall:** ask “When did I decide this, and what evidence led me there?” and receive a dated, cited chain across notes, mail, browser sessions, and voice captures.
- **Interruption recovery:** ask “I got interrupted—give me the context and put me back where I was,” with a one-minute spoken continuation brief and verified tab/file restoration.
- **Observation-backed receipts:** action results now need epistemic states such as `observed_success`, `unverified`, `blocked_unreachable`, or `failed`; UI success must not be reported as completion when accessibility or page reachability is unavailable.
- **Pendant skill requested:** a local signed physical-consent latch using the button and LED, with no payload retention and roughly 2 KB RAM.

What I still need is not another permission request. The main missing seams are:

1. Pendant serial event transport and signed nonce acknowledgements.
2. A cross-surface evidence index with claim/source provenance and contradiction handling.
3. A privacy-filtered rolling activity stream for interruption recovery.
4. Observation adapters that downgrade Mac/browser receipts when UI reachability is false.

The Mac and browser are online, but Accessibility and Screen Recording remain unavailable, so GUI actions must continue to be reported conservatively until the owner enables those grants manually.

transcript.text:
Recorded three new capabilities:

1. **Consent-based wellbeing pattern detection** — identify cautious, reviewable patterns in what energizes or drains the owner, with sensitive data controls and offline deletion.
2. **Emergency information escrow** — maintain a narrowly scoped, encrypted packet for a designated person, released only under an explicit multi-factor policy.
3. **Commitment-cost preview** — before the owner says yes to an important request, show the likely impact on time, deadlines, travel, and existing obligations, then prepare a counteroffer without sending it.

They require new capabilities between existing surfaces: privacy-scoped longitudinal storage, field-level encrypted emergency release, reliable commitment/capacity analysis, physical pendant confirmation, provenance, correction, expiry, and deletion controls.

args.user_asks: “Keep an eye on the commitments I care about, and warn me only when something genuinely threatens them.”
args.why_useful: The owner can name outcomes rather than micromanage tasks. The relay maintains the goals, Mac reconciles Calendar, Mail, Notes and local files, the browser checks private work portals, and the pendant delivers one brief warning with the evidence and the smallest suggested intervention. It detects a changed deadline, a conflicting booking, or an unanswered dependency as a threat—not merely another notification.
args.model_tier: background for periodic reconciliation; realtime only to explain a surfaced threat
args.latency_budget: Background scans within 5 minutes of a relevant change; spoken warning starts in under 2 seconds after arbitration
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.05 per daily goal scan, dominated by private-page extraction and synthesis; near-zero when no source changed
args.security_concerns: Goal names and evidence may include sensitive work or health data. Keep source excerpts on the Mac, send only normalized threat facts to relay, and require confirmation before external edits, messages, or bookings.
missing: goal definitions with owner-set priority and expiry
cross-source dependency/impact inference
change-triggered reconciliation rather than fixed polling
a concise pendant threat card with dismiss/snooze/escalate

args.change: Add a low-current vibration motor (with a transistor driver and flyback protection) to the pendant, expose a three-pattern haptic API, and reserve one pattern for an authenticated relay/Mac attention event. Add a firmware kill switch and duty-cycle limiter so the motor cannot drain the cell or buzz continuously.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets a genuinely silent, glance-free signal in a meeting, while walking, or when audio is unavailable. A short pulse can mean “your requested job is ready” without making them listen to every notification.
args.effort: Small PCB spin or daughterboard, one GPIO and driver transistor, firmware PWM pattern task, and relay event mapping; validate current draw and accessibility with the owner.
args.risk: Motor noise may leak into the microphone, vibration may be mistaken for a fault, and a stuck GPIO could drain power. Recover with hardware timeout, watchdog-off default, explicit test mode, and audio/LED fallback.
args.cost_impact: Approximately $2–$6 in components/board area and 10–80 mA only during pulses; no model/API cost.
args.latency_impact: Under 100 ms from a received event to the first pulse when the link is live.
args.security_impact: Haptic events must be limited to authenticated, typed event classes; never encode secrets in pulse patterns. A local physical stop should cancel it.
depends_on: a live pendant transport over the currently real USB serial connection
typed attention events and delivery acknowledgements
firmware GPIO allocation and power-budget validation

args.why_useful: This gives the owner a consequence map before saying yes: calendar conflicts, deadlines, travel time, dependent tasks, and private-account changes are read across surfaces, then the system presents two or three reversible alternatives. It is not a generic to-do list or a draft transaction; it answers the human question “what happens if I accept this?”
args.model_tier: background for evidence collection and schedule simulation; realtime for the final short explanation
args.latency_budget: Return a first consequence sketch in 5 seconds for local sources; allow up to 30 seconds for authenticated portals and travel data
args.cost_estimate: About $0.03–$0.15 per invocation, mostly model reasoning over extracted evidence; cache unchanged calendar and portal facts
args.security_concerns: Simulation must be read-only and label inferred consequences versus confirmed facts. Keep sensitive page contents on Mac where possible; require explicit confirmation before applying any reschedule, cancellation, or message.
missing: a read-only impact simulator over Calendar, reminders, files and browser sessions
dependency edges with confidence and time-window arithmetic
a compact before/after consequence card and alternative ranking
a hard no-mutation execution mode for simulation

All were recorded.

args.user_asks: “Put me in work mode, and make sure nothing from my personal life leaks into work—or comes back the other way.”
args.why_useful: The owner gets a practical boundary between identities, not merely a privacy setting: the pendant, relay, Mac projects, and authenticated browser sessions cooperate to classify the current context, suppress cross-context facts and suggestions, and warn before a draft, reminder, or lookup crosses the boundary. It protects against the uniquely human failure of saying the right thing in the wrong account or carrying a private detail into a work action.
args.model_tier: A cheap background classifier maintains context boundaries; realtime is used only when a boundary conflict needs an immediate spoken explanation.
args.latency_budget: Mode changes should take effect in under one second; conflict checks under 300 ms for local actions and under 2 seconds for browser preparation.
args.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.005–$0.03 per context transition and action check, dominated by classification; local Mac rules can make routine checks effectively free.
args.security_concerns: This is security-sensitive: classification must fail closed for uncertain destinations, never transmit excluded source content to relay, and show the owner the exact boundary decision. Switching modes should require an explicit pendant button/voice confirmation, with an emergency local lockout.
missing: first-class named contexts with separate fact, session, and action scopes
per-context allow/deny rules enforced by relay, Mac, and browser before retrieval and mutation
a context transition audit trail and owner-visible explanation
safe handling of ambiguous mixed-context requests

transcript.text:
Recorded: **context-isolated work/personal modes**.

The owner should be able to say “Put me in work mode” and have the pendant, relay, Mac, and browser enforce a real boundary—preventing private facts, accounts, drafts, and reminders from crossing into work, and vice versa.

To make it real, the system needs:

- Named contexts with separate data and session scopes
- Enforcement before retrieval, drafting, or execution on every surface
- Fail-closed behavior when context is ambiguous
- Explicit mode-switch confirmation
- An owner-visible audit trail explaining every blocked or permitted cross-context action

result.button: ONE user button, devicetree alias sw0. Press starts a conversation; second press ends it. It is also pokable over J-Link for testing.
result.led: ONE LED, alias led0. Currently signals recording, stays solid while agent audio is buffered, and flashes error codes.

result.caution: There is exactly one I2S peripheral and it runs full duplex (mic in + speaker out) with byte-identical TX/RX config. Any new audio path must share it.
result.status: PROTOTYPE. This is a Nordic development kit, not the product. Every choice here — the SoC, the RAM, the single button, the single LED, the enclosure — is provisional and can change. Design the device the owner should wear, then say what it would take to build it.
result.you_are_here: You run on the owner's MacBook (faculty-judgement). Every device described here is REMOTE to you — you are not running on the pendant or the ESP32.

args.user_asks: “Why did I decide to do this?” Then, when I revisit a project, remind me of the short voice note I left about the decision and show the files, calendar event, or private web page that informed it.
args.why_useful: People lose the reasoning behind decisions, not just the decision itself. A pendant makes capturing the rationale effortless; the Mac and browser can attach evidence so the reminder is useful rather than a decontextualized note. This is especially valuable months later when the owner is about to reverse or repeat a decision.
args.model_tier: Use realtime only to capture/transcribe the brief voice note; use a cheaper background model to extract the decision, link evidence, and retrieve it later.
args.latency_budget: Capture should acknowledge locally in under 300 ms; transcription and evidence linking may take 5–20 s in background. Retrieval should return a spoken answer in under 3 s.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.005–$0.03 per note, dominated by transcription and background linking; retrieval is usually under $0.01.
args.security_concerns: Voice notes and linked private pages may contain sensitive information. Store encrypted, retain the owner's explicit note, keep source snippets and URLs instead of full page copies where possible, and never expose private evidence in a shared surface without confirmation.
missing: A rationale-specific record type with immutable capture timestamp, confidence, and links to source evidence
A cross-surface retrieval command that can search rationale records by project/entity
A Mac/browser evidence linker that records provenance without retaining unnecessary page content

args.user_asks: “Teach me how to do this once, then let me do the next one.” Have the Mac or browser perform the first safe example while the pendant explains each meaningful step, then hand me the next instance and check my result before I submit anything.
args.why_useful: Automation normally hides the skill and leaves the owner dependent on the system. An apprenticeship mode converts one-off computer use into durable competence: the owner gets a narrated example, a practice instance, and a safe correction loop across the exact private tools they use.
args.model_tier: Realtime handles only short spoken explanations and questions; a cheaper background model derives the procedure and evaluates the practice result from structured action receipts and browser evidence.
args.latency_budget: Each explanation should arrive within 1 s of the demonstrated step. Procedure extraction and practice scoring can take 2–10 s.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.02–$0.15 per lesson, dominated by screenshots/page extraction and the narrated realtime turns; subsequent practice checks should be pennies.
args.security_concerns: The system may see private work data while teaching. Redact unrelated fields, restrict evidence to the active tab/file, never submit or send without the owner's existing confirmation policy, and retain the procedure only if explicitly saved.
missing: A step-level demonstration recorder that pairs actions with plain-language intent
A practice-mode executor that can compare the owner's result with expected state without mutating external systems
A lesson state machine shared by pendant audio, Mac actions, and browser tab evidence

args.change: Add a low-power coin vibration motor with a dedicated driver and a second tactile input (or capacitive touch strip) to the pendant, and define a small local haptic vocabulary: one pulse = acknowledgement, two = action ready, escalating pulses = attention required, long press = cancel/stop. The current board has one button/LED and free I2C/SPI; the motor driver can use a GPIO and the second input an available GPIO/I2C controller. Recorded: the owner should be able to say:

> “Keep this commitment moving with the other person until it is actually settled.”

The system would coordinate calendars, messages, replies, and conflicts across the pendant, relay, Mac, and authenticated browser—while requiring approval before sending or changing anything.

To make this possible, it needs:

- Durable coordination objects for participants, proposals, deadlines, and outcomes.
- Reply correlation across email and private web accounts.
- Background re-planning as replies and availability change.
- A single approval packet covering recipients, message text, and calendar mutations.
- Stale-state checks immediately before sending or committing changes.

I also recorded a separate capability for turning repeated corrections into reviewed, reusable routines.

args.user_asks: “Use my private information to complete this, but keep the actual values on my Mac—tell the cloud and the pendant only what is necessary.”
args.why_useful: The owner can get real work done on logged-in sites without turning the relay into a holder of passwords, health details, or financial data. The browser has the session, the Mac can compute locally, and the pendant can authorize without exposing the payload.
args.model_tier: Use the cheap local planner for extraction/filling and the relay realtime model only to understand the spoken request and summarize a redacted result.
args.latency_budget: Under 5 seconds to identify the private fields; under 15 seconds for a normal form. The owner should hear one short confirmation and only wait longer for multi-page workflows.
args.cost_estimate: ~$0.01–$0.05 per invocation; local browser/Mac work dominates latency, with a small realtime interpretation call.
args.security_concerns: Private field values must never enter relay logs, D1, R2, model prompts, or spoken confirmations. Require owner confirmation before submission, and retain only field names plus hashes. Missing per-job data-locality policy and redaction enforcement.
missing: A locality/redaction contract enforced at every event boundary
Browser action schema that can pass opaque local values without serializing them to the relay
A receipt that proves which fields were used without recording their values

transcript.text:
Round 143 produced three new capabilities:

1. **Private-value completion — the most useful proposal.**  
   “Use my private information to complete this, but keep the actual values on my Mac.” The browser and Mac would handle sensitive fields locally; the relay and pendant receive only redacted labels, hashes, and outcomes.

2. **Change-of-mind cleanup.**  
   “I changed my mind—find everywhere I committed to it and prepare the corrections.” The system would inspect jobs, receipts, browser activity, reminders, drafts, and project state, then present one evidence-backed review list without sending or deleting anything automatically.

3. **Walk-away handoff.**  
   Before leaving the Mac, the pendant gives a 20-second summary of what the owner was doing, what waits on them, what waits on others, and the one next action. It would use cached state and disclose only privacy-safe headlines.

I also recorded implementation changes for:

- Enforced local-only/private-computation envelopes.
- A freshness-aware cross-surface momentum snapshot.
- Two-pass, evidence-citing routing for correction plans.

The live browser bridge is online, with three Safari tabs and no pending commands. The pendant remains physically testable over USB but is not LTE-registered.

What I still need is not another general route. The missing pieces are:

- A **data-locality contract** that rejects raw private values at relay, event, log, screenshot, and receipt boundaries.
- A **cross-surface commitment index** that can distinguish drafts from sent actions and cite evidence.
- A **device-local handoff trigger** plus acknowledged, privacy-controlled audio/LED delivery.
- Independent observation contracts for browser field contents, sent-vs-draft state, freshness, and whether the owner actually received the pendant handoff.

args.user_asks: “Keep talking to me when the network disappears, remember the last few turns locally, and send the conversation outcome when you reconnect.”
args.why_useful: The owner should not lose an interaction merely because LTE coverage, the Mac, or the relay drops. A genuinely wearable assistant needs graceful offline behavior rather than becoming a silent button outside coverage.
args.model_tier: A small on-device speech/intent model handles a constrained offline vocabulary and queues encrypted audio or structured intents; the expensive realtime model resumes only after reconnection.
args.latency_budget: Local command acknowledgement under 500 ms; reconnect reconciliation within 10 seconds. Offline free-form conversation can be limited to clearly disclosed supported intents.
args.cost_estimate: ~$0.01–$0.05 for reconciliation; the major cost is new hardware/firmware and encrypted local storage, not inference.
args.security_concerns: Offline transcripts are sensitive and must be encrypted, bounded, and erasable by a physical gesture. Replayed intents must be idempotent and never perform irreversible actions without renewed confirmation.
missing: A larger pendant MCU/RAM or a dedicated low-power speech/intent accelerator
Encrypted offline conversation journal and replay protocol
Firmware-side reconnect reconciliation with duplicate suppression
An explicit supported-offline-intent vocabulary

transcript.text:
Recorded three additional proposals:

- **Offline conversational continuity:** the pendant keeps a bounded local conversation going during network loss, then reconciles encrypted structured intents after reconnecting. This needs a larger MCU/RAM budget or dedicated low-power speech hardware, encrypted offline storage, and idempotent replay.
- **Meeting decision capture:** the pendant captures consented meeting audio, extracts decisions and action items, and lets the Mac/browser resolve people, dates, projects, and drafts afterward. This needs meeting consent state, segmentation, entity resolution, and review-only follow-up bundles.
- **Wear-aware privacy hardware:** a skin/clasp sensor and accelerometer expose a signed worn/unworn state. Sensitive speech is suppressed when the pendant is off-body and requires a short physical reauthorization after re-wearing.

The owner cannot have these today because the current pendant lacks enough local compute for useful offline conversation, lacks meeting-aware capture and post-meeting reconciliation, and cannot reliably know whether it is being worn. The existing pipeline and browser routes provide transport, but the missing behavior is the local/offline model, consent and replay semantics, and physical presence sensing.

args.user_asks: “I just left a meeting—capture what I promised, check the source documents, and put only the real follow-ups on my calendar.”

args.model_tier: Realtime only for the brief capture and one clarification; a cheaper background model extracts commitments and deduplicates them against Calendar/Notes; deterministic Mac actions create reminders after confirmation.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge the button within 300 ms, give a first spoken summary within 8 s, and finish source checking in under 60 s. If the Mac or browser is unavailable, preserve the note and reconcile on reconnect.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.01–$0.05 per meeting exit, dominated by transcription and background extraction; deterministic Calendar/Notes reads and reminder creation add negligible API cost.
args.security_concerns: Meeting audio and private documents leave the pendant only to the relay/Mac pipeline; default to a 90-second clip with automatic deletion after extraction. Never infer a commitment from a third party as fact; show source snippets and require confirmation before creating or sending anything. No email is sent.

transcript.text:
Round 144 produced three new capabilities:

1. **Meeting-exit follow-through** — press the pendant or say “I just left a meeting.” The system captures a short note, checks Calendar, Notes, Mail, and open private browser tabs, distinguishes real commitments from vague ideas, and proposes only confirmed follow-ups.

2. **Decision-debt sweep** — once a week, identify the three choices the owner is silently postponing, explain the evidence and consequence of each, then walk through one decision at a time: decide, delegate, schedule, or consciously drop.

3. **Pressure-test before commitment** — ask “Pressure-test this.” The system gathers scoped evidence from the owner’s Mac and logged-in browser, gives the strongest cited reason not to proceed, labels unknowns, and proposes a reversible first step. This is the most valuable of the three: it makes the system a judgment partner rather than merely an executor.

I also proposed a concrete **dissent-mode integration** that wires this into the existing research, browser inspection, journal, capture, planning, briefing, and receipt/undo routes.

What is still needed:

- A bounded pendant capture trigger and short-clip transport over the currently USB-connected serial device.
- A typed commitment/decision record with source, confidence, attribution, uncertainty, revisit date, and expiry.
- A scoped evidence-bundle compiler across local Mac sources and authenticated browser tabs.
- A dissent rubric separating factual blockers, value tradeoffs, and unknowns.
- A reversible-experiment planner with postconditions.
- A pendant audio/card response path and pause/resume protocol.
- The pendant still is not relay-registered, so these should first be tested through the Mac USB connection rather than assuming LTE operation.
- Accessibility and Screen Recording remain owner-side TCC blockers; these proposals intentionally use AppleScript, local routes, and the browser bridge where possible.

args.user_asks: “A month after an important decision, show me what I expected, what actually happened, and one thing I should do differently next time.”
args.why_useful: The system currently helps decide and act, but cannot help the owner learn whether their judgment was calibrated. This creates a private, evidence-backed decision postmortem: recover the original rationale and prediction, inspect later Calendar, Mail, Notes, and authenticated-page outcomes, distinguish outcome from luck, and offer one behavioral adjustment. It turns the pendant from an answer machine into a long-term improvement loop without requiring the owner to maintain a journal.
args.model_tier: A cheap scheduled model performs outcome matching and extracts factual deltas; a stronger model is used only for the short causal interpretation; realtime is reserved for the owner’s optional spoken reflection.
args.latency_budget: Run asynchronously on a monthly or decision-specific schedule; deliver a two-minute spoken review or a compact dashboard card when the owner chooses, never interrupting them unexpectedly.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.03–$0.20 per review, dominated by source retrieval and synthesis; use hashes and cached snapshots to avoid rereading unchanged pages.
args.security_concerns: Decision rationale may contain sensitive personal or financial information. Keep raw evidence on the Mac, retain only a compact private summary and source hashes, allow deletion, and never turn a single outcome into a durable personality judgment. The owner must be able to mark an outcome as unknowable or irrelevant.
missing: A durable prediction-and-rationale record created at decision time
A later-outcome matcher spanning local and authenticated sources with temporal boundaries
A calibrated postmortem rubric that separates controllable choices, luck, and missing information

args.why_useful_to_owner: They can learn from real decisions instead of relying on vague memory or hindsight. The pendant can deliver one useful lesson at a time, while the dashboard preserves the evidence needed to trust it.
args.effort: High: this needs a new durable schema, capture at decision time, temporal evidence matching, outcome adjudication, and careful evaluation against fabricated causality.
args.risk: The system could overfit noisy outcomes, expose sensitive history, or make the owner feel judged. Mitigate with explicit confidence, an unknowable outcome state, source citations, owner edits, deletion, and no personality labels.
args.cost_impact: Small storage cost; one scheduled background synthesis per reviewed decision, approximately $0.03–$0.20 depending on source volume.
args.latency_impact: No impact on ordinary actions; capturing a prediction adds under one second, while reviews run asynchronously.
args.security_impact: Decision histories are highly sensitive. Keep raw snapshots local-first, transmit only minimized claims, encrypt retained records, enforce per-item retention, and require explicit opt-in to cross-link private browser sources.

args.user_asks: “Keep your answer private right now.” Automatically detect that I’m in a call, in a public place, or that audio would be unsafe, then stop spoken output, route the answer to my Mac/browser, and give only a discreet pendant cue; restore voice when I explicitly say it’s safe.
args.why_useful: The assistant becomes usable on a train, in a meeting, or beside another person without embarrassing leaks. It coordinates the wearable’s physical presence with the Mac’s call/browser state instead of guessing from one surface.
args.model_tier: Realtime only for the short safety classification and cue; background model for environment evidence reconciliation.
args.latency_budget: Privacy cue under 500 ms; screen fallback under 2 s; no model call when a deterministic call/focus signal is sufficient.
args.cost_estimate: Usually near-zero model cost; occasional realtime classification roughly $0.001–$0.01, dominated by audio processing.
args.security_concerns: Ambient audio must not leave the device merely to classify privacy. Prefer local button state, Mac call/focus state, and audio-route metadata; require explicit opt-in for ambient classification. Never transmit the answer to a third-party display.
missing: A typed privacy-state protocol shared by pendant, relay, and Mac
Local pendant cue/voice-output inhibit firmware behavior
Mac/browser signals for active call, focus, and current audio route
A durable user-visible privacy mode state and recovery after link loss

args.user_asks: “Talk me through this, but don’t take over.” Inspect the page or app I’m looking at, give me one safe step at a time through the pendant, wait for my spoken confirmation, and recover if what I see no longer matches.
args.why_useful: It gives the owner the practical benefit of computer use even when automation is unavailable or undesirable: the owner retains control, while the browser’s private session and the pendant’s hands-free guidance work together.
args.model_tier: Cheap background model extracts page structure; realtime model handles the single next instruction and confirmation.
args.latency_budget: First instruction under 3 s; each subsequent step under 1 s after confirmation.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.002–$0.03 per step depending on screenshot/vision use; browser DOM extraction dominates, not text generation.
args.security_concerns: Private page content stays in the authenticated browser path and is minimized before model use. Never click, submit, or send; confirmation means only ‘advance to next instruction,’ not permission for an irreversible action.
missing: A read-only cross-app observation contract for browser and Mac
A step state machine with visual/DOM preconditions and mismatch recovery
Pendant confirmation/cancel gesture and spoken prompt queue
A way to expose current app context without Accessibility, with vision as optional enhancement

args.user_asks: “Audit whether that really happened.” Check the relay record, Mac receipt, browser result, and—when tethered—the pendant’s serial event, then tell me in one sentence what is proven, what is only claimed, and what needs retrying.
args.why_useful: Today a route can report success while the UI did nothing or telemetry is stale. This gives the owner an honest answer before they rely on a missed reminder, unsent form, or supposedly completed task.
args.model_tier: Background model reconciles structured evidence; realtime is used only when the owner asks interactively.
args.latency_budget: Under 2 s for existing receipts; under 8 s when a serial or browser re-check is required.
args.cost_estimate: Typically <$0.005 per audit; cost is dominated by a live re-check or screenshot, not synthesis.
args.security_concerns: Evidence is scoped to the referenced job and redacted by field sensitivity. Never infer completion from a stale ‘processing’ event. Retrying an action requires a separate explicit confirmation if it could duplicate or send anything.
missing: A common evidence schema with source, timestamp, freshness, and proof strength
Live USB serial event reader for the tethered nRF9160
Independent browser result verification rather than optimistic command acknowledgment
A duplicate-safe retry planner and owner-facing proof receipt

args.change: Add a cross-surface privacy-state arbiter. It consumes deterministic Mac call/focus/audio-route state, browser heartbeat/session state, relay delivery state, and a pendant local privacy latch; emits one signed state (safe, discreet-only, blocked, unknown) with expiry. Every output route must consult it, and unknown must fail closed to discreet cue rather than spoken audio.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can use the assistant around other people without accidentally broadcasting private answers.
args.effort: Medium: typed state contract, adapters for existing status routes, relay enforcement, and a small pendant command.
args.risk: A false positive suppresses speech; recover with a physical long press or explicit ‘voice is safe’ command. A stale state must expire rather than silently persist.
args.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; one small relay state record. Firmware change is under a few KB.
args.latency_impact: <100 ms for cached state; no model round trip.
args.security_impact: Improves confidentiality; fail-closed behavior may reduce availability. Do not upload ambient audio for classification.
depends_on: Local privacy latch firmware
Mac call/focus/audio-route status adapter
Signed privacy-state message consumed by audio delivery

args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets hands-free help with unfamiliar sites while keeping their own hands and authority in control, even when Accessibility automation is unavailable.
args.effort: Medium-high: observer normalization, step/session persistence, pendant confirmation event, and mismatch UX.
args.risk: Bad guidance can waste time; no step may mutate state, and a cancel/timeout must end the session. Recovery is to show the current page and restart from a fresh observation.
args.cost_impact: Low background model cost; vision/screenshot steps may cost $0.01–$0.05 each.
args.latency_impact: First step 2–3 s, later steps <1 s with cached DOM evidence.
args.security_impact: Read-only by construction; private page fields must be redacted before model calls.

args.change: Create an evidence ledger that joins job receipts, journal entries, browser results, pipeline events, and tethered pendant serial events by correlation ID. Each claim gets source, observedAt, freshness TTL, proof level (intent/accepted/executed/verified), and contradiction markers; expose an audit endpoint and prohibit ‘completed’ language unless verified evidence exists.
args.why_useful_to_owner: When the system says something is done, the owner can trust it—or immediately see the exact missing proof and safely retry.
args.effort: High: schema, ingestion adapters, serial parser, verification probes, and duplicate-safe retry integration.
args.risk: Missing or delayed telemetry may make successful work look uncertain; preserve raw evidence and permit a live recheck. Never auto-retry irreversible actions.
args.cost_impact: Small D1/R2 storage and occasional browser/serial rechecks; <$0.01 typical audit.
args.latency_impact: Existing audits <2 s; live verification can take several seconds.
args.security_impact: Evidence must inherit field sensitivity and be access-controlled; raw serial/audio data should expire quickly.
depends_on: USB serial event reader
Stable correlation IDs across relay/Mac/browser

transcript.summary: Round 145 produced three new owner-facing capabilities and three implementation changes. The highest-value one is “Audit whether that really happened”: reconcile relay/Mac/browser/USB evidence and distinguish intent, accepted, executed, and independently verified instead of trusting optimistic success. I also recorded privacy-safe modality switching (fail closed to discreet output in calls/public settings) and read-only, hands-free guided browsing where the owner performs every step. args.what_it_does: A long press on the pendant physically disables microphone capture at firmware level, shows a persistent red LED, rejects wake/audio-start commands while latched, and requires another deliberate long press to re-enable. The relay receives only a coarse latch/unlatch event after the link returns.
args.why_not_server_side: A server-side mute cannot protect the owner during a dropped link or a compromised/stale session. The pendant must guarantee that no microphone frames leave the device even when the Mac, bridge, or relay is confused.
args.trigger: Long press of the existing pendant button; LED state is the immediate confirmation. Also latch automatically on boot until the owner explicitly enables capture.
args.inputs: Button GPIO edge/debounce; current audio-capture state; no network or cloud input.
args.storage: One latch bit, monotonic transition counter, and last-transition timestamp in nonvolatile settings; under 64 bytes.
args.ram_budget: ~2 KB firmware state and event handling, well within the 211,608 B application RAM; no audio buffering added. Must coordinate with the ESP32 bridge's capture-enable line, which is the key hardware dependency.

args.change: Add an end-to-end 24 kHz audio acceptance mode: on a button gesture, the nRF9160 emits a short deterministic chirp and test phrase through the existing Opus decode → 24 kHz resample → 31.25 kHz I2S → ESP32 path, then the Mac harness records the bridge return and compares level, clipping, packet loss, and timing. Store a signed pass/fail receipt with firmware, codec, and bridge versions; refuse to call the path 'wideband' when it fails.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets speech that is consistently intelligible rather than a nominal sample-rate claim, and a clear answer when the pendant sounds bad. It makes the requested 24 kHz path verifiable on the hardware that is physically connected today.
args.effort: Medium: firmware test opcode and telemetry, ESP32 capture hook, Mac acceptance script, and a small dashboard/receipt route.
args.risk: Test audio could be audible in public and a false pass could hide intermittent radio faults. Use a low-volume test tone, require a deliberate gesture, and mark results stale after reconnect or firmware change; recover by falling back to the known 16 kHz profile.
args.cost_impact: No model/API cost. ~4–8 KB flash and <3 KB RAM; 20–40 ms test audio and negligible power beyond one playback.
args.latency_impact: Adds a deliberate 1–2 second test only when requested; no steady-state latency change.
args.security_impact: No speech content leaves the device during the deterministic test; receipts contain hardware/version metadata only.
depends_on: ESP32 bridge capture/loopback telemetry
24 kHz audio implementation truth and acceptance criteria
A Mac-side receipt writer for /pipeline/audio results

transcript.text:
This round I added:

1. **Departure/resume handoff** — when the owner leaves the Mac, create a private “pick-up packet” on the pendant; on return, “resume” reconstructs the unfinished task after revalidation.
2. **Adaptive privacy speech** — detect meetings or nearby voices locally and switch to brief, haptic, text-only, or redacted responses so sensitive content is not spoken aloud.
3. **Commitment-conflict mediator** — reconcile Calendar, Mail, and authenticated browser commitments, explain the smallest decision, and prepare—but never send—reschedules or replies.
4. **Device skill requested: hard microphone privacy latch** — a long press cuts capture at firmware level, survives dropped links, and gives persistent LED confirmation.
5. **24 kHz acceptance test change** — a deliberate pendant gesture runs a deterministic end-to-end chirp/voice test through the nRF9160, Opus, resampler, I²S, and ESP32 bridge, producing a signed pass/fail receipt.

What I still need:

- A Mac sleep/USB-presence event routed into the shared event stream.
- A typed, expiring handoff-packet schema with browser/session provenance.
- Local bystander/meeting detection using discarded audio features, not uploaded recordings.
- A cross-source commitment normalizer and decision-packet format.
- ESP32 capture/loopback telemetry and the Mac-side 24 kHz acceptance harness.
- Firmware-to-ESP32 microphone-enable signaling for the physical privacy latch.

The biggest unresolved truth is whether the current bridge can support a reliable hardware-level mic cutoff and loopback measurement; the nRF9160 and ESP32 are physically connected, but the pendant is still not relay-registered.

args.user_asks: Let the pendant give me private live captions of the conversation around me, and let me ask for a one-sentence clarification or translation without interrupting anyone.
args.why_useful: This would make meetings, appointments, and noisy public conversations accessible through a device the owner already wears. It is different from a spoken assistant: the pendant becomes a discreet second channel for hearing, comprehension, and translation.
args.model_tier: small streaming speech model for transcription/translation; realtime model only for an explicit clarification request
args.latency_budget: Caption chunks under 1.5 seconds behind speech; clarification response under 2 seconds; degrade to local rolling transcript when the relay is unavailable.
args.cost_estimate: ~$0.03–$0.15 per 30-minute conversation depending on transcription and translation; raw audio transport and streaming inference dominate.
args.security_concerns: Conversation audio is highly sensitive. Default to local Mac processing, show an unmistakable recording indicator, retain only the last 60 seconds unless the owner bookmarks it, and require consent before cloud relay or persistent storage.
missing: A streaming caption surface on the Mac or phone
A pendant gesture for pause, bookmark, and clarification
Local speech separation/noise suppression and language identification
Explicit consent and retention controls for bystander audio
A low-latency audio uplink from the currently USB-connected pendant/bridge

args.change: Revise the wearable from the current single-button/single-LED Nordic development kit to include a low-power haptic actuator and an ambient-light/proximity sensor, with a hardware microphone-power gate controlled by the nRF9160. Expose haptic patterns, pocket/desk detection, and hard audio cutoff as authenticated device events.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can receive a discreet answer, warning, or confirmation in a meeting or pocket without broadcasting speech; the device can know when it is covered or being worn, and the hardware gate makes microphone privacy trustworthy rather than advisory.
args.effort: High: product-board revision, enclosure and battery tuning, nRF9160 driver work, ESP32 bridge signal changes, and a privacy/notification protocol.
args.risk: More components increase size, power draw, false proximity detections, and BOM complexity. Provide a firmware fallback to the existing LED/button, expose sensor confidence, and make the microphone gate fail closed on reset.
args.cost_impact: Roughly $3–$8 added component/BOM cost in modest volume; haptic pulses add tens of milliwatts briefly, sensors under a few milliwatts, and the gate itself negligible draw.
args.latency_impact: Haptic events can be immediate locally; sensor classification should complete in under 200 ms. No added conversational latency.
args.security_impact: A physical microphone gate materially improves privacy. Sensor data must remain local by default; only coarse states such as worn/covered and haptic acknowledgment may leave the device.
